title: Data Systems and Business Intelligence Officer (80%) - deadline extended
source: The Global Community Engagement and Resilience Fund
body:
Position title: Data Systems and Business Intelligence Officer

Team: Performance and Impact

Required FTE: 80%

Required travel: Some travel, up to 10% of time

Reports to: Head – Performance and Impact

**Scope of the role**

Violent extremism is a direct threat to international security, economic growth, and development. GCERF works to prevent violent extremism by investing in people. As the only global fund dedicated to preventing violent extremism (PVE), we connect local communities to global resources and support grassroots initiatives that are often out of reach for international donors. We fund community-centric initiatives led by civil society organisations to address the local social, economic, and political drivers of violent extremism.

The Data Systems and Business Intelligence Officer will be part of GCERF’s dynamic and high-performing team of Monitoring and Evaluation experts. This role is responsible for managing, maintaining, and expanding the data infrastructure and systems, with a focus on grant performance and programmatic information, including descriptive, predictive, and prescriptive analytics.

**Principal accountabilities and ownership**

**Data Architecture, Integration and Infrastructure:** Responsible for designing, maintaining and improving GCERF’s data architecture, databases and (automated) ETL pipelines, connecting grant management, programme, results and financial data. Monitor system performance, reliability, access and scalability, and coordinate the resolution of integration and technical issues

**Grant Management System and Data Product Ownership:** Responsible for functional development of the data and results components in Salesforce, including requirement gathering, user acceptance criteria and testing, and leading historical data migration initiatives into the CRM.

**Data Quality and Documentation:** Responsible for establishing data definitions, business glossaries, calculation logic and SoPs across systems. Maintain system documentation, user guidance, data marketplace documentation, and administrative manuals to support self-service analytics.

**Business Intelligence, Analytics and Reporting:** Responsible for designing and maintaining user-centred dashboards and analytical products in Power BI or other approved platforms. Produce and interpret data on organisational KPIs, grants and portfolio performance for management, the Governing Board and donors, documenting sources, methods, calculations and limitations.

**Artificial Intelligence:** Explore practical uses of AI and automation in data processing, validation, retrieval, analysis and reporting, while also supporting pilot projects.

**Knowledge/Experience/Qualifications**

- Strong experience with IT and Business Intelligence tools (Python, SQL, Linux/Unix, Tableau, MSOffice/PowerBI), with at least five years of previous, progressive experience in a similar role.
- Excellent report-writing skills.
- Fluency in English; working knowledge of French is an advantage (B2-level). Russian and Arabic are also an asset.
- Master’s degree in Economics, Data Science, Statistics, International Relations, Social Sciences, or a related field.
- Experience integrating AI into data systems is an asset.
- Previous experience or demonstrated interest in the prevention of radicalisation to violent extremism will be an asset.
- Detail-oriented, excellent coordination skills, must be able to work independently and have a keen interest in seeking tech solutions to improve efficiency.

**Values**

Demonstration of alignment with GCERF’s key values is a critical component of the selection process:

Make a difference

Achieve together

Uphold integrity

Respect yourself and others

Learn and improve

Be Kind

**Personal attributes based on GCERF competencies**

Be proactive

Work collaboratively

Be accountable and drive for solutions and results

Communicate effectively

Embrace learning and entrepreneurial spirit

**General information**: Our office is located in Geneva, Switzerland. Swiss residency or work eligibility is not a requirement.

GCERF values diversity, equality and inclusion, and we hire globally. We are committed to hiring qualified candidates irrespective of age, disability, ethnicity, national origin, family status, sex, gender identity or expression, physical characteristics, race, religion, spirituality or sexual orientation. GCERF has a zero tolerance policy towards sexual harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, as well as any form of discrimination or harassment. GCERF stands by its commitment to welcoming persons of all backgrounds into a safe work environment.

All selected candidates will undergo rigorous reference checks and anti-terrorism screening.

Contract: 1 year, renewable. Part-time (32 hours per week). The arrangement of days and hours worked is flexible.

GCERF allows a limited number of remote working days per week.

Competitive compensation package.

title: Regional Coordinator, Programme - Danish RC
source: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies
body:
## **Organizational Context**

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world’s largest humanitarian network, with 191-member National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. IFRC uses the Triple R – response, resilience and respect – to deliver on Strategy 2030. IFRC responds to disasters and crises, ensuring timely, coordinated and locally led humanitarian action. IFRC supports its members in building community resilience in the areas of climate and environment, health and wellbeing, and migration and displacement. IFRC promotes respect for our fundamental principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality, including in our work on values, power and inclusion. The IFRC focuses throughout on our core mandate – our raison d’être – of strategic and operational coordination, humanitarian diplomacy, National Society development, and accountability.  
IFRC is led by its Secretary General and has its Headquarters in Geneva and five regional offices in Africa (Nairobi); the Americas (Panama); Asia Pacific (Kuala Lumpur); Europe (Budapest); and MENA (Beirut) as well as representation offices, service centres and delegations across the globe.

The IFRC has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and other forms of harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, and lack of integrity (including but not limited to financial misconduct). IFRC also adheres to strict child safeguarding principles.

DRC has been present in the Middle East & North Africa (MENA) region since 2002 and is implementing projects with National Society partners in Syria, Lebanon, Iraq, Yemen and oPt, and is working towards three main breakthroughs: 1) Healthy lives, 2) Disasters damage fewer lives and 3) Included and safe people.

The DRC Regional management is led by the Head of MENA, HoR Deputy and MENA HR manager. The management team ensures overall prioritization and leadership and is accountable for progress according to contractual and legal obligations. The regional management team ensures productive relations and alignment with Red Cross and Red Crescent movement and external partners.

## **Job Purpose**

The post-holder will be responsible for the day-to-day coordination and implementation of regional programmes and projects, working closely with the relevant Country Managers and country delegates, particularly in relation to the implementation of the NCD programme. The role will provide guidance and support to programme implementers and facilitate coordination with relevant programme and technical colleagues, with a particular focus on regional programmes in North Africa. The post-holder will also support country teams throughout the project cycle, including needs assessments, project design, implementation, monitoring and reporting.

## **Job Duties and Responsibilities**

Programme design and development (15%)

- Lead the strategic and innovative development of all relevant programme documents, especially but not limited to regional programs such as NCD and P2P
- Facilitate and coordinate assessments, baseline and end-line studies, mid-term reviews and evaluations for programme management and development.
- Organize, host and brief relevant technical assessment/evaluation missions, and communications visits.
- Facilitate NCD research initiatives together with the DRC NCD technical team, DRC country teams and NSs.
- Be involved in relevant NCD / P2P network in the region and with relevant RC partners, UN partners and other NCD actors.
- Ensure a strong focus on adaptive learning and evidence-based knowledge management.

Programme management (50%)

- Ensure implementation of country projects for the NCD and other regional initiatives on track, and that funds are utilized in accordance with budgets / plans, in close cooperation with the rest of the relevant Country Office Teams.
- Maintain an overview of the programme and corresponding country projects and alert Technical NCD leader or Deputy Head of Region if there are issues of concern.
- Participate in and contribute to the bi-monthly DRC Regional PPFU meeting and coordinate with Finance Officer for the programme as well as those related to North Africa.
- Support all programme reporting, including the annual Project Progress Reports (PPR) process – are completed on time and at high quality, allowing for technical reviews in advance of submission.
- Ensure consolidated programme reports are submitted to donors on time.
- Conduct field level programme monitoring in coordination with the relevant DRC CMs and NSs Specially on NCD and P2P programs
- Contribute to the DRCs effort to engage in wider coordination with relevant thematic activities in-countries and/or at regional level
- Consolidation results across all project locations and serves as the central point for overall reporting requirements (NCD)

## **Job Duties and Responsibilities (continued)**

Capacity building of implementing partners (15%)

- Establish strong working relationships with the DRC country teams and help identify areas of support in the implementing NSs.
- Support implementing partners to strengthen their capacity for improved Health technical and Project Monitoring, Evaluation and Reporting (PMER) and learning and innovation skills.
- Provide programme management support to Country Offices, including temporary gap-filling support when required.
- Guide and support programme implementers and facilitate coordination with relevant programme and technical colleagues, particularly for regional programmes in North Africa.

Programme coordination and visibility (10%)

- Coordinate with key stakeholder internal or external to ensure the connection of the regional programmes.
- Represent the programme in relevant national, regional, and international fora
- Ensure visibility of the programme based on captured LL
- Facilitate capacity building and knowledge sharing for Integrated programme initiatives and processes, including trainings, at regional and national level as per require in coordination with DRC HQ colleagues.

General programme support (10%)

- Support DHoR in preparing key documents, operational project documents and country project agreements.
- Explore fundraising possibilities for regional programmes related interventions and innovative development in coordination with the DHoR.
- Analyse, coordinate and support the feasibility of implementing programmes in North Africa.
- Perform any other relevant duty assigned by the DoHR

## **Education**

Required

- Relevant academic degree or equivalent experience from the field

Preferred

- Knowledge on any other thematic areas such as Disaster Risk Management, Migration, protection will be considered as an asset

## **Experience**

Required

- A minimum of 7 years of actual field experience in programme management or related project implementation.
- Proven experience in programme management in developing and/or conflict-affected countries.
- Information management and analytical skills, in assessment, project design, and programme financial management.
- Coordination skills, with an emphasis on working through and building the capacity of national partners.

Preffered

- Relevant post-graduate university degree in Health preferably or equivalent studies
- Experience of working in the Middle East in development or humanitarian contexts.
- Experience of working within the Red Cross/Red Crescent Movement
- Experience in narrative and financial reporting and proposal writing

## **Knowledge, Skills and Languages**

Required

- Self-supporting in computers (Email, Internet, spread sheets, word-processing, etc.)
- Excellent communication, organization and facilitation skills
- Confidence in situations of occasional stress, and able to handle a substantial but varied workload for a long period.
- Results-orientated and self-motivated but at the same time a patient, cooperative, innovative, and flexible team player.
- Understanding that process and ownership are key to achieving results in culturally and politically sensitive environments.
- Excellent diplomacy, communication, coordination, negotiation, networking, and facilitation skills.
- Demonstrated core proficiency in (a) digital communication & collaboration, (b) basic digital content creation, (c) digital safety & security, (d) data literacy, and (e) problemsolving with technology (including responsible use of AI assistants.
- Understanding of and commitment to IFRC’s mission and values.
- Fluent spoken and written English

Preferred

- Good command of another IFRC official language (French, Spanish or Arabic)

## **Competencies, Values and Comments**

- Values: Respect for diversity; Integrity; Professionalism; Accountability
- Core competencies: Communication; Collaboration and teamwork; Judgement and decision making; National society and customer relations; Creativity and innovation; Building trust

A confirmation email will be sent to you upon submitting your application. Please ensure that you verify your email address using the link provided in the email; otherwise, your application will not be received and, therefore, cannot be considered or assessed.

**The closing date and time for this vacancy are based on Geneva time. Applications must be submitted by 23:59 (11:59 PM) Geneva time on the advertised closing date.**

**IFRC Disclaimer**  
*IFRC has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and other forms of harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, and lack of integrity (including but not limited to financial misconduct). IFRC also adheres to strict child safeguarding principles.*  
*If you appointed to or undertake a role within IFRC, whether as staff, staff on loan or secondees, you will be subject to the organization's Code of Conduct, which is available here and on our website.*  
*Note: All offers of employment will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which include prior professional conduct checks and review of criminal records. IFRC will request a conduct check from all prior employers for a period of 5 years, including but not limited to employers who like IFRC participate in the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme. For more details on the Scheme, please see ont-style: italic;">THE MISCONDUCT DISCLOSURE SCHEME — SCHR.*  
*IFRC ensures equal employment opportunities!*

title: National Consultant (Climate Mobility Research and Data)
body:
Overview of position

**Nature of the consultancy:**

**Deliverable Based Consultancy (output-based)**

Research, data, consultation and in-person facilitation support to the International Consultant for the gender-sensitive Climate Mobility Needs Assessment and Country Diagnostic for Somalia and for the co-creation and validation of the Climate Mobility Programme for integration into the NDC 3.0 Investment and Implementation Plan, where feasible.

**Project Context and Scope:**

**Background**

Recurrent droughts, floods and environmental degradation, combined with fragility and conflict, drive large-scale human mobility and displacement in Somalia. The National Adaptation Plan (NAP 2.0, 2026–2030) and the Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC 3.0) both recognise human mobility in the context of climate change as a priority. However, limited consolidated data and institutional capacity make it difficult to turn these commitments into investment-ready interventions, and human mobility is not yet well reflected in the NDC 3.0 Investment Plan 2025–2030 launched by the Ministry of Environment and Climate Change (MoECC) at COP 30. The MoECC has asked the client to help address this.

This consultancy is part of the client’s Development Fund project “Strengthening Climate Mobility Investment Readiness in Somalia: Advancing NAP and NDC Implementation”, under Output 1.1 (Climate Mobility Needs Assessment and Country Diagnostic) and Output 1.2 (Climate Mobility Programme).

Role objectives

**Working arrangement**

The assignment is delivered by two consultants working as one team. The **International Consultant** (home-based) leads the technical work and presents online at all workshops (unless travel is confirmed). The **National Consultant** (Somalia-based) starts one month earlier to compile data and map stakeholders, supports the data collection and consultations and organizes and facilitates all workshops and events in person, with logistical support from the client’s project team. All work is carried out with the MoECC and its Inter-Ministerial NDC Taskforce. The client’s Climate Action Department and Regional Climate Action Unit (Nairobi) provide technical support and quality assurance.

**Main tasks**

Under the supervision of the client and the day-to-day technical guidance of the International Consultant, the National Consultant will:

**Data and evidence:** compile a literature review and secondary data (climate, socio-economic, displacement and human mobility) from national and international sources, and complete a stakeholder mapping.

**Consultations:** adapt and translate (English/Somali) the KII/FGD guides developed by the International Consultant, and conduct consultations with government, technical agencies and communities, including women and girls and other vulnerable groups.

**Workshops and events:** organize and facilitate in person, with logistical support from the client’s project team and the International Consultant presenting online: (i) the inception workshop; (ii) a combined workshop to validate the Country Diagnostic and co-create the Climate Mobility Programme; and (iii) the Programme validation workshop. Provide interpretation, minutes and a consolidated summary of feedback for each.

**Coordination with the MoECC:** support a climate mobility working group under the existing Inter-Ministerial NDC Taskforce, and liaise with the MoECC to obtain and compile relevant information on the NDC 3.0 Investment and Implementation Plan, where feasible.

**Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing:**

Community Stabilization Unit, Transition and Recovery Pillar (TRP), the client.

Project: “Strengthening Climate Mobility Investment Readiness in Somalia: Advancing NAP and NDC Implementation” – project code SO10P0800, funded by the client’s Development Fund (IDF).

**Tangible and measurable outputs** **of the work assignment**

The National Consultant will deliver the following outputs on a three-instalment payment basis. Months refer to the months of this contract (Month 1 = the month the Consultant starts); the International Consultant starts in Month 2:

**Deliverable 1 – Workplan and Stakeholder Mapping (max. 10 pages).** – Deliverable by email by mid-Month 1.

**Deliverable 2 – Literature Review and Secondary Data Compilation (max. 20 pages, plus dataset):** ready for the International Consultant when they start in Month 2. – **First instalment payment (Deliverables 1–2)** – Deliverable by email by end of Month 1.

**Deliverable 3 – Inception Workshop and Stakeholder Consultations Report (max. 20 pages):** inception workshop facilitated in person (end of Month 2) with minutes; translated tools; consultations conducted and findings summarized. – Deliverable by email by end of Month 3.

**Deliverable 4 – Validation and Co-Creation Workshop:** workshop facilitated in person in late Month 4 to validate the Country Diagnostic findings and co-create the Climate Mobility Programme; minutes and consolidated results. – **Second instalment payment (Deliverables 3–4)** – Deliverable by email by end of Month 4.

**Final Deliverable 5 – Programme Validation Workshop:** workshop facilitated in person (mid-Month 6); minutes and consolidated feedback for the final Programme; compiled information on the NDC 3.0 Investment and Implementation Plan, where feasible. – **Third and final instalment payment** – Deliverable by email by end of Month 6.

Each deliverable may go through more than one draft; it is considered complete once the client’s feedback has been incorporated and the client has approved it.

**Performance indicators for the evaluation of results**

Deliverables submitted on time and approved by the client.

Data compilation and consultations complete, well-sourced and inclusive of women, girls and other vulnerable groups.

All three workshops held as planned, with MoECC and Taskforce participation, and minutes and feedback delivered within one week.

Effective coordination with the International Consultant and the client’s project team.

**Payment terms and conditions**

Lump-sum fee paid in three instalments against approved deliverables:

**First instalment – 25% :** Deliverables 1–2 – Workplan and Stakeholder Mapping; Literature Review and Secondary Data Compilation (Month 1).

**Second instalment – 50% :** Deliverables 3–4 – Inception Workshop and Consultations Report; Validation and Co-Creation Workshop (Month 4).

**Third and final instalment – 25%:** Deliverable 5 – Programme Validation Workshop (Month 6).

Payments are released upon the client’s approval of the respective deliverables, together with a short progress report (achievements, challenges, lessons learned and recommendations against the approved workplan), and are subject to satisfactory confirmation by the Programme Manager. The fee is all-inclusive.

Team management

There is no team management under this role.

Further information

**Experience**

Bachelor’s with 3 years of relevant professional experience or Masters with 1 year of relevant professional experience in human rights, migration, displacement, climate change, environmental governance, or development programming.

Demonstrated experience organizing and facilitating workshops and consultations with government counterparts and communities is required.

Experience in data collection, literature review, synthesis of secondary data, and policy research and analytical writing.

Experience working with displaced and vulnerable communities (e.g., IDPs, refugees, migrants).

Experience with NDC/NAP processes or climate finance (e.g., Green Climate Fund, Global Environment Facility) is an asset.

**Skills and languages**

Strong facilitation, communication and stakeholder engagement skills.

Ability to draft clear research summaries, consultation reports and meeting minutes.

Knowledge of the Somali context and of gender and protection approaches in climate and mobility programming.

Fluency in Somali and English (written and spoken) is required.

title: Grants, Partnerships and Communication Coordinator
body:
***This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.***

***Fluency in both English & Spanish required***.

***Funding until September 30, 2027, potential to extend***.

**BACKGROUND**

Venezuela continues to face a protracted humanitarian crisis. Inside the country, millions of people have limited access to food, health care, safe water and other essential services, and needs are most acute among people on the move and returnees, Indigenous communities, women and girls at risk of gender-based violence, and children at risk of acute malnutrition. In 2026, an earthquake affecting La Guaira, Miranda and Caracas added new humanitarian needs. At the same time, more than 7 million refugees and migrants have left Venezuela, making this one of the largest external displacement crises in the world, with Colombia hosting the largest number of them.

In Colombia, the escalation of the internal armed conflict has deepened humanitarian needs. Disputes between non-state armed groups over territorial control are driving forced displacement, confinement, movement restrictions, the recruitment of children and adolescents, and gender-based violence, particularly in border and Pacific regions such as Norte de Santander and Nariño. The crisis in Catatumbo alone, which began in January 2025, has displaced more than 100,000 people. Mixed migration flows continue in several directions, including Venezuelans in transit and pendular movements across the border, as well as reverse flows of people returning south from Central and North America and returns to Venezuela, which add complexity to the response.

The IRC is addressing these needs through an integrated, population-based response in Colombia and Venezuela, covering health (including sexual and reproductive health and mental health), protection and women’s protection and empowerment, child protection, multipurpose cash and economic recovery, nutrition, water, sanitation and hygiene, and education. The IRC employs a mixed modality, providing lifesaving services directly and with local partners, and in Venezuela a significant share of funds is channeled through local organizations. Activities are financed by a diverse portfolio of donors, including ECHO, Sida, GFFO, OCHA-managed pooled funds (such as the Venezuela Humanitarian Fund and the Regional Humanitarian Pooled Fund for Latin America and the Caribbean), the Disasters Emergency Committee, UN agencies and private foundations, among others.

**Purpose of the role:** IRC Colombia and Venezuela is seeking an experienced business development, grants, and partnerships professional for the role of Grants, Partnerships and Communications Coordinator. This role is responsible for leading resource mobilization and the timely production of high-quality funding proposals, modification requests and donor reports; playing a lead role in the full award management cycle, including compliance; facilitating partnership development and management processes; leading the communications strategy that positions the IRC’s work with donors, partners and the public and protects the organization’s reputation; and coordinating grants management-related capacity building efforts among IRC staff and partners. The Grants, and Partnerships Coordinator ensures the quality of and efficient processes for proposal development and grants management, and manages the delivery of the IRC’s partnership ambitions while supporting program coordinators and country leadership to ensure that IRC Colombia and Venezuela lives up to the partnership principles of responsibility, results-oriented approaches, equality, transparency, and complementarity.

The postholder will need to work under tight deadlines and deal with competing and changing priorities. The postholder will need to gather inputs by influencing other functions and roles while submitting quality and timely deliverables, will work with diverse country, region and headquarters-based teams, and will need to ensure adherence to organizational and donor compliance requirements. The position will be based in Bogota with frequent visits to field sites in Colombia and Venezuela.

**Scope and authority:** The Grants, Partnerships and Communications Coordinator will lead a team of 15 members (both direct and indirect) divided in three sub-teams: grants, partnerships, and communications. The postholder will line manage 6 direct reports.

**Key Accountabilities & responsibilities:**

***Business Development and Resource Mobilization:***

- Lead the development and annual update of a resource mobilization strategy for IRC Colombia and Venezuela, aligned with the country Strategy Action Plan, with clear targets by donor, sector and geography.
- Manage the funding pipeline: investigate and track funding opportunities, maintain an up-to-date pipeline tracker, and regularly report on its status to country leadership.
- Lead the Go/No-Go analysis for each opportunity, assessing strategic fit, competitiveness, implementation capacity, risks, cost recovery and compliance requirements, and facilitate timely decisions with country leadership.
- Drive donor diversification and positioning beyond traditional institutional donors, including pooled funds (such as the Venezuela Humanitarian Fund and the Regional Humanitarian Pooled Fund), multilateral agencies and development banks, the private sector and foundations, and funding dedicated to localization and to partnerships with local organizations.
- Lead program design workshops for new business development opportunities with relevant IRC staff, and partners’ staff where applicable.
- Develop, lead, and track proposal development processes, including consortium proposals, directly coordinating and managing the development of proposals and concept notes in collaboration with multiple departments and stakeholders; write sections of proposals and conduct final reviews, editing, and polishing of proposal documents for accuracy and quality control.
- Assist in compiling and editing proposal budgets and ensure communication and coordination between all departments (finance, programs, and operations) in drafting of budgets, bringing a strategic and competitive lens to the process.

***Grants/Sub-Grants Management:***

- Ensure that IRC awards and sub-awards in Colombia and Venezuela are well-administered and implemented in compliance with the relevant donor regulations and IRC procedures throughout the full award cycle.
- Lead award start-up, including grant summaries and kick-off meetings (pre-award and opening meetings) with programs, finance, operations and partners, so that all teams understand donor requirements from the outset.
- Lead the review and negotiation of grant and sub-grant agreements, in coordination with the Awards Management Unit, finance and other relevant departments.
- Coordinate award modifications, including cost and no-cost extensions, budget realignments and changes in scope, ensuring timely submission and donor approval.
- Take the lead on internal and external reporting in coordination with programs, MEAL, and finance, ensuring high-quality, well-written and timely reports meeting donor and IRC requirements. Maintain close collaboration with all relevant departments in preparation of donor reports.
- Maintain award tracking systems, including the grants tracker, reporting and deadline calendars and award dashboards, ensuring that information is accurate and available to budget holders and senior management.
- Supervise the GPU in the coordination and facilitation of project cycle meetings.
- Lead award close-out processes, ensuring that final reports, financial reconciliation, asset disposition and documentation are completed on time.
- Coordinate the preparation for and follow-up of donor audits, verifications and monitoring visits, including the implementation of their recommendations.
- Play a significant role in efforts to strengthen and maintain country program project management capacities.
- Ensure that sub-grantees are being monitored for donor compliance and progress against objectives, and that key compliance monitoring information and learning are documented.
- Assist program technical leads, operations staff, and partners with understanding the reporting and other compliance requirements on their grants and sub-grants.
- Proactively identify compliance risks throughout the portfolio and advise programs, operations, finance and senior management on necessary actions.

***Partnerships Management:***

- Play a lead role in stakeholder analysis and potential partner mapping and vetting.
- Working closely with other senior staff, play a lead role in identifying, liaising on, and negotiating teaming arrangements with potential partners; collaborate with other departments as needed to verify and issue various types of partnership agreements.
- Ensure and coordinate adherence to IRC’s Partnership Excellence for Equality and Results System (PEERS) in the selection and management of IRC Colombia and Venezuela’s partnerships.
- Co-lead the review of the performance of different partnerships, including successes, challenges and lessons learned.
- Support country leadership in promoting an enabling environment for effective work in partnership.
- Provide a quarterly Partnership Management Report to the CD, incorporating input from technical coordinators and operational leads as appropriate.

***Staff management and capacity building***

- Maintain a broad and deep understanding of donor policies, regulations, and procedures and build this knowledge among grants team members.
- Build grant management capacity of field staff, and provide supportive supervision in report writing, budget management, indicator tracking, IRC-specific tools, and other topics as/if needed.
- Maintain open and professional relations with team members, promoting a strong team spirit and providing oversight and guidance to enable staff to successfully perform in their positions.
- Maintain documentation of institutional knowledge and program activities in coordination with relevant sector coordinators and department leads.

***Communications***

- **Communications strategy:** Lead the development and implementation of a communications strategy for IRC Colombia and Venezuela, aligned with the country strategy, resource mobilization priorities and IRC regional and global communications.
- **Brand management and visibility:** Ensure consistent and appropriate use of the IRC brand across materials, events, field sites and partner activities; provide advice on donor visibility requirements and proactively engage with program teams to ensure appropriate IRC and donor visibility.
- **Creation of communication materials:** Lead Colombia and Venezuela’s efforts in designing, writing and editing key communication materials (factsheets, capacity statements, stories from the field, digital content or special reports on IRC’s activities) in coordination with DDPs, program leads, and sector and field coordinators.
- **Crisis communications and reputational risk:** Develop and maintain protocols for crisis communications and reputational risk management, and advise the CD and senior management on sensitive issues, including security, data protection and the political context in Colombia and Venezuela.
- **Internal communications:** Promote clear and timely internal communication across offices and teams in Colombia and Venezuela, so that staff are informed about the country program’s priorities, results and key decisions.
- **Media:** Support media and communications activities in coordination with IRC regional and global communications teams, ensuring the safety, dignity and informed consent of clients.
- **Advocacy:** Support the CD and DDPs as needed.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Country Director, Colombia and Venezuela

**Position directly supervises:** Grants, Partnerships and Communications Unit staff

**Other Internal and/or external contacts:**

**Internal:** Venezuela Country Manager and Venezuela senior management team, with whom the postholder works closely on the Venezuela portfolio; Colombia/Venezuela Deputy Directors of Programs and leads of programs, Finance and Operations, Budget Officers/Managers, HR Lead, Access & Security Department; MEAL Unit; Awards Management Unit (Regional), regional partnerships advisor, regional and global communications teams, and Technical Advisors.

**External:** Donors and pooled fund managers, consortium partners, local partner organizations, UN agencies and humanitarian coordination mechanisms, other NGO counterparts and media, as needed and indicated by Country Director, Country Manager or Deputy Director of Programs.

**Qualifications**

- Bachelor’s degree in relevant discipline, Master’s degree desired.
- At least five years international work experience in humanitarian and development programs; experience in a similar position/role is desired.
- Demonstrated, successful experience in program design and writing proposals for public and private donors.
- Solid knowledge of donor rules and regulations, including ECHO, Sida, GFFO, UN agencies and OCHA-managed pooled funds; knowledge of other European, multilateral and private donor requirements is an asset.
- Demonstrated experience managing the full award cycle, including compliance, modifications, audits and close-out, and in managing partnerships with local organizations.
- Experience in communications, brand management or external relations in a humanitarian or development organization is desirable.
- Demonstrable understanding of project planning and management cycles.
- Highly organized, close attention to detail, and ability to effectively prioritize tasks in a fluid environment.
- Demonstrable high-level performance management and team-working skills, and well developed negotiation skills.
- Highly developed interpersonal, communication and relationship skills, with the ability to influence and represent the organization with external organizations and stakeholders.
- Effective people- and program-management skills in acute emergency contexts: can train and lead staff productively under stressful circumstances.
- Flexible, focused and reliable, with the ability to work well under administrative and programmatic pressures in an environment of changing demands.
- Experience in the region is an asset; knowledge of the Colombian and Venezuelan contexts is strongly desired.
- Digital literacy and strong computer skills: MS Word, Excel & email applications required.

**Language Preference**

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English and Spanish, with high quality copywriting and editing skills in both languages.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate around: 10,051,500 COP/monthly). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

title: Call for Supplier Prequalification: Various Goods and Services (RFP-2026-EA-007)
body:
**Tender details**

- **Issuing agency**Doctors Without Borders / Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF), Nairobi, Kenya
- **Invitation**Qualified companies, firms or consortiums are invited to apply for **Supplier Prequalification for Various Goods and Services**.
- **Reference number**RFP-2026-EA-007
- **Key dates**Confirmation of participation: 18 November 2026  
    Final questions: 25 November 2026  
    **Bids due: 2 December 2026**  
    Shortlisting: 9 December 2026  
    Optional interviews: 16 December 2026  
    Final selection: 23 December 2026
- **How to submit**Send separate Technical and Financial proposals by email to **msfea-proc-tenders@nairobi.msf.org**. Bids must pass mandatory screening, then technical evaluation, before any financial proposal is opened.

**Open categories**

[https://msf.or.ke/rfp-2026-ea-007-supplier-prequalification-various-goods-and-services](https://msf.or.ke/rfp-2026-ea-007-supplier-prequalification-various-goods-and-services)

- [**TOR-005**Reverse Osmosis (RO) and Ultrafiltration (UF) Systems Maintenance Services**→**](https://msf.or.ke/rfp-2026-ea-007-terms-reference-005-reverse-osmosis-ro-and-ultrafiltration-uf-systems-maintenance)
- [**TOR-006**Waste Management Services**→**](https://msf.or.ke/rfp-2026-ea-007-terms-reference-006-waste-management-services)
- [**TOR-007**Website Migration and Improvement Consultancy**→**](https://msf.or.ke/rfp-2026-ea-007-terms-reference-007-website-migration-and-improvement-consultancy-msf)
- [**TOR-008**Framework Supply of Office Stationery, Pantry and General Consumables**→**](https://msf.or.ke/rfp-2026-ea-007-terms-reference-008-framework-supply-office-stationery-pantry-and-general)
- [**TOR-009**Awareness and Fundraising Campaign, Marketing Agency Services**→**](https://msf.or.ke/rfp-2026-ea-007-terms-reference-009-awareness-and-fundraising-campaign-marketing-agency-services)
- [**TOR-010**Cleaning and Related Facilities Services**→**](https://msf.or.ke/rfp-2026-ea-007-terms-reference-010-cleaning-and-related-facilities-services)
- [**TOR-011**Assessment of Radiation Impacts from the Rooftop Antenna Mast to the 5th Floor, Pitman House](https://msf.or.ke/rfp-2026-ea-007-terms-reference-011-assessment-radiation-impacts-rooftop-antenna-mast-5th-floor)

## **Introduction & Overview**

- **Doctors Without Borders/Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)** is a private international association providing assistance to populations in distress, victims of natural or man-made disasters and victims of armed conflict.
- **MSF observes neutrality and impartiality** in the name of universal medical ethics and the right to humanitarian assistance, and maintains independence from political, economic or religious powers.
- **MSF staff:** About 65,000 people worldwide, with more than 90 percent recruited in the countries where programmes run, across doctors, nurses, midwives, surgeons, logistics, water and sanitation, administration and support staff.
- **MSF Eastern Africa (MSFEA)** is an institutional member of MSF focused on representation and networking, recruiting and supporting staff from the region, communications and fundraising, plus dossiers including Diversity, Equity and Inclusion, Data Protection, mutualization, training, medical operational support and environmental health.
- **MSF operates in over 70 countries** and the movement is composed of over 25 associations worldwide in 2026.

## **Purpose and Objectives**

- **Invite qualified suppliers to prequalify** for the supply of goods and provision of services across various categories outlined in the Terms of Reference.
- **Select suppliers through a structured process** using separate Technical and Financial proposals, with value placed on brief, precise and customized statements.
- **Ensure transparent and fair competition** with the same information shared with all bidders if MSF adds or clarifies information.
- **Build a pool for future contracting** while MSF reserves the right to accept or reject any bid, stop the process at any time, or enlarge or reissue an RFP process.

## **Scope, Lots and Eligibility**

- **Scope:** Supplier prequalification for various goods and services for MSF Spain (Eastern Africa).
- **Lots:** Bidders apply per lot as defined in the attached Terms of Reference. The main RFP does not list the lots. Check the applicable ToR for your lot.
- **Who can apply:** Qualified companies, firms or consortiums. Local companies registered in the country of the project cannot appear as joint venture or associate partners in more than one application.
- **Response language:** English only.
- **Bid validity:** Bids must remain valid for at least 90 days after submission.

## **Required Services & Submissions**

- **Goods and services:** As specified per lot in the attached Terms of Reference. The main RFP refers all technical service detail to the ToR.
- **Technical proposal must show** that the ToR and its objectives have been fully understood, and that proposed methods and resources match the detailed needs.
- **Presentation:** Clear, complete and readable. Diagrams, tables and graphs may be included as necessary.
- **Financial proposal:** Detailed commercial offer, itemized per the technical proposal, and must follow the standard pricing schedule in the ToR.

## **ICT, Technical & Evaluation Standards**

- **No separate ICT or audio visual standard in this main RFP.** Technical criteria are detailed in the Terms of Reference for each lot.
- **General technical standard:** Brief, precise and customized statements. Clear, complete and readable presentation.
- **Proposal structure:** Two separate folders or digital documents. One marked TECHNICAL PROPOSAL, one marked FINANCIAL PROPOSAL.
- **Separation rule:** No financial information in the technical proposal. Financial proposals remain sealed until technical evaluation is completed.

## **Safety, Security, Health and Accessibility**

- **Safe and hygienic working environment:** Suppliers are expected to ensure a safe and hygienic environment, take steps to prevent accidents and injury, and minimize hazards inherent in the working environment.
- **Labour rights:** No forced, slave, indentured or involuntary prison labour. No child labour. Fair payment per International Labour Organization rules. Fair treatment with respect, dignity and non discrimination.
- **Human rights and behaviour:** Respect internationally proclaimed human rights. No discrimination, physical or psychological abuse, exploitation of vulnerability, child abuse, or inappropriate conduct for personal gain.
- **Anti corruption and illegal activity:** No fraud, bribery, illicit activities or financing of illicit activities. Declare conflicts of interest immediately in writing and end the conflict as soon as reasonably possible. Ensure no party is subject to economic and trade sanctions.
- **Environmental protection and sustainability:** Monitor and reduce environmental impact, source responsibly, reuse and recycle, reduce packaging and energy use, use renewable energy, minimize air and water pollution, and use responsible product formulation. MSF aims to reduce CO2 emissions by 50 percent by 2030 and to create social added value through its suppliers.

## **Confidentiality and Data Protection**

- **RFP confidentiality:** The RFP and any information disclosed or obtained during the RFP must be treated as Confidential Information. Do not share with third parties or use for any purpose other than preparing a response without prior consent from MSF Eastern Africa.
- **Evaluation confidentiality:** Information relating to examination, clarification and evaluation of bids, and the state of the process, is strictly confidential.
- **Non disclosure agreement:** Bidders may be asked to sign a Non Disclosure Agreement if deemed necessary.
- **Confidentiality clause:** All MSF information, including missions, operations and medical treatment of any patient, is confidential. Use only for execution of obligations. Do not publish, disclose or retain copies without prior written consent. Return copies on request and destroy files at the end of the agreement. Obligations survive for 10 years from termination.
- **Data protection:** Kenya Data Protection Act of 2019 applies. MSF is the Data Controller and the Service Provider is the Data Processor. Do not use data for other purposes, do not disclose it, train staff with access, apply technical and organisational safeguards, get prior specific written authorisation before using another processor, and forward data subject requests to MSF as soon as received. In the event of a data breach, immediately inform MSF at dpo@nairobi.msf.org.

## **Minimum Qualification Requirements**

- **Mandatory requirements, pass or fail:** Failure to submit any one document, or submission of an expired or invalid document, disqualifies the proposal from technical and financial evaluation.
- **Mandatory list:** Certificate of registration. Current CR12 Certificate confirming partners, directors and shareholding, not older than 6 months, where applicable. Valid Tax Compliance Certificate. Copy of KRA PIN Certificate. Valid business permit. Any other mandatory requirement highlighted in the Terms of Reference.
- **General information required:** Organisation name, correspondence address, contact name and position, telephone, email, website, registered office address, number of employees who can be involved at technical level, parent company details if part of a group, and partnerships, alliances or agreements with other companies.
- **Financial information required:** Bank name, address, telephone and contact, Company Registration Number, VAT Registration Number if VAT registered, annual turnover in KSHs for latest year and one year previous, payment currency, and payment terms. Form states 30 days after submission of invoice, with space for Other.
- **Client references:** State how many references can be contacted in total and provide the 3 most relevant references, with organisation, contact, scope, implementation duration, description, date and main challenges faced.

## **Framework Agreement and Booking Mechanism**

- **No obligation to buy:** Issuing the RFP does not imply any obligation for MSF to buy any goods or services offered. All bidder costs for responding and for subsequent negotiations are borne by the bidder.
- **Award:** Successful bidder is informed in writing through a formal notification of award. MSF will then send the draft contract. Selected bidder is expected to agree to use MSF standard template. If not possible, MSF may involve its legal department.
- **Contract signing:** Within 30 working days of notification of award, the successful tenderer will sign, date and send back the contract. If not, MSF can consider the award null and void after official notification.
- **Unsuccessful bidders:** Informed by email within 15 working days following the award.
- **MSF rights:** MSF reserves the right to revise or amend RFP terms before the submission deadline and share modified documents with all invited bidders. MSF also reserves the right to deselect a tenderer if capacity is deemed not adequate or compatible with the tender dossier.
- **Financial ranking:** Financial proposals are opened and scored only for technically qualified firms. Assessment is on total adjusted price excluding customs and excise duties, taxes, levies and similar in Kenya after correcting arithmetical errors and deducting items not to be included. For comparison, total adjusted price is converted to Kenya Shillings at the exchange rate of the day. Ranking is by highest number of points. MSF may award the highest scoring bidder or create a short list of top scoring bidders.

## **Deliverables, Reporting and Acceptance**

[msf.or.ke](https://msf.or.ke/sites/default/files/2026-11/RFP-2026-EA-007-Supplier%20Prequalification-Various%20goods%20and%20services%20%282%29.pdf)

- **Submit by email:** Send responses and related documents to msfea-proc-tenders@nairobi.msf.org by 2 December 2026 at the latest. Reference the RFP reference and lot number in the email subject line. Late proposals will be rejected and returned or discarded.
- **Confirm participation:** Send written confirmation of participation by email by 18 November 2026.
- **Clarifications:** Enquiries only in writing, no later than 25 November 2026. Confirmation of receipt will be sent by email to all bidders in a circular letter. Project information visits only if outlined in the Terms of Reference.
- **Two part submission:** Technical offer plus Financial offer as detailed in Section 3.7, plus signed annexes.
- **Signed annexes required:** Signed copy of the RFP document with completed tables 4.2, 4.3 and 4.4. Signed copy of the attached ToR as applicable. Signed copy of Supplier Code of Conduct. Signed copy of Data Protection Agreement. Signed copy of MSF Charter.
- **Annexes list:** MSF Charter. MSF Supplier Code of Conduct. MSF Data Protection and Confidentiality. Terms of References.

title: 23305 Programme Manager (Immigration and Border Governance, Migration Governance, and Labour Mobility) (P)
Human Resources Manager
body:
**Starting position: January 1, 2026**

**Duration : 12 months**

**Place of work : Damascus, Syria**

**Status : National contract, fixed- term**

**Deadline for applications:** Terre des hommes does not set a deadline for applications for this position, recruitment is open until the position is filled.

Terre des hommes (Tdh) :

The Terre des hommes Foundation (Tdh), with headquarters in Lausanne and an office in Zurich, is the leading Swiss child rights organisation with more than 2000 employees worldwide. We stand together with children to uphold their rights, protect their lives and improve their well-being. We achieve this through innovative programmes focused on health, migration and access to justice, specially designed to have a positive and sustainable impact.

**Context :**

The HR Manager is responsible for providing strategic leadership and operational management of all Human Resources functions within Tdh Syria. This role ensures that the delegation is staffed with qualified, competent, and motivated personnel who actively contribute to improving the lives of children and their families. As a key member of the Senior Management Team, the HR Manager plays a pivotal role in shaping organizational culture, promoting staff engagement, and aligning HR practices with Tdh’s mission and strategic objectives. The position oversees workforce planning, recruitment, performance management, staff development, and employee relations, while ensuring compliance with Tdh’s Global Code of Conduct, internal policies, Child Safeguarding standards, and HR procedures. In addition to strategic responsibilities, the HR Manager manages core administrative functions such as payroll, leave administration, contract management, and benefits, ensuring accuracy, transparency, and adherence to local labor laws and organizational policies. Furthermore, the HR Manager works to build the capacity of HR staff at mission level, fosters a safe and respectful work environment, and supports managers in applying best practices in people management. Ultimately, this role serves as a trusted advisor to leadership and staff, ensuring that HR systems and processes enable the organization to achieve its humanitarian goals effectively and ethically.

**Main responsibilities:**

**HR Strategy & Governance**

- Translate operational and institutional needs into local HR strategies aligned with Tdh’s global People Strategy.
- Provide strategic input on workforce planning, organizational design, and talent needs.
- Conduct HR organizational assessments and propose improvements.
- Ensure Tdh’s values and safeguarding principles are respected.
- Contribute to building an HR information system, and provide analysis to inform and improve HR related decision making processes.

**Policy, Compliance & HR Framework**

- Develop, update, and implement HR policies and SOPs in line with local labor law and global standards.
- Ensure compliance with staff regulations, labor laws, and internal governance standards.
- Oversee data protection, confidentiality, and compliant personnel record management.
- Deliver training to managers and staff on HR policies and compliance requirements.

**Workforce Planning & HR Operations**

- Oversee recruitment, hiring, onboarding, and workforce planning processes.
- Ensure accurate payroll checks and compliance with HR operations.
- Conduct or contribute to salary and benefits benchmarking; advise on compensation and reward strategies.

**Performance Management & Talent Development**

- Implement and monitor performance management systems and processes.
- Support goal setting, coaching, and career development initiatives.
- Prepare annual capacity building plans aligning with Tdh’s strategic objectives.
- Promote continuous feedback and staff development opportunities.

**Employee Relations, Engagement & Well-Being**

- Act as focal point for employee relations, including grievances, disciplinary processes, and mediation.
- Promote open and constructive dialogue between employees and management.
- Foster a positive, inclusive, and psychologically safe workplace.
- Promote mental health support and psychosocial well-being initiatives.
- Organize team building activities.

**Budget & Compliance**

- Monitor HR budgets, staffing costs, and FMT allocations.
- Ensure Staff archving is complete and uploaded to respective HR country folders.

**Crisis Management**

- Anticipate HR needs in crisis contexts, including surge capacity and duty-of-care measures.
- Act as HR focal point during emergencies, ensuring timely workforce deployment and staff well-being.
- Coordinate with Operations, Security, and Staff Health during crises.

**External Relations & Representation**

- Liaise with legal advisors, labor authorities, and HR networks.
- Represent Tdh in HR forums and conduct sector benchmarking to maintain best practices.

**Core Competencies:**

- Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple HR and administrative tasks with a results-oriented approach.
- Strategic thinking and ability to align HR initiatives with organizational goals.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English and Arabic.
- Strong interpersonal skills to work effectively with employees at all levels and maintain positive professional relationships.
- High attention to detail, accuracy, and thoroughness in documentation, data entry, and filing.
- Ability to plan, prioritize, and follow up on tasks efficiently, especially under tight deadlines.
- Confidentiality and professionalism in handling sensitive employee information and HR documentation.
- Good understanding of HR procedures, recruitment steps, and administrative workflows.
- Self-motivated, proactive, and able to work independently and as part of a team, with flexibility and adaptability to changing operational needs.
- **\*\*The full Job Description will be shared with shortlisted candidates.\*\***
    
    **Profile :**
    
    **Education :** Bachelor’s degree in human resources, Business Administration, Economics, or a related field; a master’s degree is an asset.
    
    **Experience / Skills :**
- Minimum of five years of professional experience in Human Resources, with at least two years as head of an HR department.
- At least two years of experience within an NGO is required.
    
    **Languages :**
    
    Fluency in Arabic and English is required.
    
    **IT knowledge :**
    
    Proficiency in MS Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook) and ability to work with HR systems and digital archiving.
    
    Experience working with an HRIS is an advantage.
    
    Salary :
    
    As per Tdh Salary scale in Syria.

**Tdh General Code of Conduct and Ethical Policies** :

- Commits to promoting and complying with the Global Code of Conduct, systematically reporting any violations of the Code through Tdh's formal reporting mechanisms and dealing with any violations of procedures and processes appropriately.
- Raises awareness of the Foundation of the risks of policy non-compliance, violence and abuse, and related rights, towards children, community members and our own employees.
- Undertakes to comply with key ethical policies and guidelines, including the Safeguarding Policy, the Anti-Fraud and Corruption Policy, the Conflict-of-Interest Policy and other policies related to the prevention of terrorist financing and criminal activities, as well as workplace behavior.
- Commits to putting values and principles into practice through exemplary behavior, in full compliance with the Code of Conduct, and always respecting established procedures and processes.
- Commits to developing a compliant and enlightened management culture within the organization and in our work with children and the communities in which we operate.

**Procedure:**

Only complete applications (CV + covering letter) posted on our official website will be processed. Additional documents (diplomas, work certificates, etc.) will be requested at a later date. We will only contact those candidates selected for further recruitment.

**References :**

Please note that all job offers will be subject to satisfactory references and checks (criminal record and anti-terrorism funding check). Terre des hommes will ask the Human Resources of previous organisations to provide references on any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment as well as fraud and corruption, during employment, or incidents under investigation at the time the candidate left employment.

title: ICT Officer
body:
Plan International is an independent child rights and humanitarian organisation committed to children living a life free of poverty, violence and injustice. Plan actively unite children, communities and other people who share our mission to make positive lasting changes in children’s and young people’s lives. Plan support children to gain the skills, knowledge and confidence they need to claim their rights to a fulfilling life, today and in the future. Plan place a specific focus on girls and women, who are most often left behind. Plan have been building powerful partnerships for children for more than 80 years and are now active in more than 70 countries. Plan International Jordan is established in 2016 and has programmes in governorates in the centre, north and south regions as well as host communities and Azraq camp.

**Role PURPOSE**

The ICT Officer reports to the Head of Operations and Finance and is responsible for providing IT support to staff, and for maintaining the IT infrastructure of the office according to Plan's policies and procedures. The role supports the management of IT assets, networks, devices and servers, and implements ICT standards, security and policies within Plan Jordan.

**Dimensions of the Role**

 The ICT Officer will be responsible for supporting and following on Operational ICT policies, goals, objectives and guidelines and for the ICT planning and implementation. Specifically, s/he will support the Head of Operations and Finance in leading an effective administration, procurement of IT assets , services and ICT Road Map and plans, supervise and/or implement the necessary administration, procurement & logistics processes to ensure the purchase and delivery of ICT supplies and capital equipment in line with the approved response budget.

The role encompasses a broad range of responsibilities, including the effective management and tracking of IT assets, maintenance of ICT infrastructure, and provision of timely technical support to staff to ensure smooth and efficient operations.

**Accountabilities**

**ICT Duties:**

1\. ICT Infrastructure and Systems Administration

- Administer, maintain, and support PIJO's ICT infrastructure, including servers, networks, storage systems, hardware, software, and related technology resources, ensuring reliable and efficient operations.
- Install, configure, maintain, and troubleshoot Windows Server environments, including Active Directory (AD), DNS, DHCP, Group Policy (GPO), file services, print services, and user profiles.
- Manage and maintain virtualized server environments using Microsoft Hyper-V, including virtual machines, resource allocation, and system availability.
- Administer and maintain network infrastructure, including LAN, WAN, wireless networks, switches, access points, routers, and network connectivity.
- Configure, manage, and monitor network security appliances, including Cisco Meraki MX Firewall, security policies, traffic filtering, intrusion detection and prevention, and network access controls.
- Manage and troubleshoot VPN connectivity and remote access services, ensuring secure access to organizational resources in accordance with approved security policies.
- Monitor internet connectivity, network performance, bandwidth utilization, and ISP services, coordinating with telecommunications providers to resolve service interruptions.
- Administer and monitor wireless network infrastructure, including access point configuration, connectivity, coverage, and performance.
- Maintain and support CCTV systems, including cameras, recording devices, monitoring systems, and associated network connectivity.
- Monitor the performance, availability, and capacity of ICT infrastructure and recommend corrective or preventive actions to minimize service disruptions.
- Maintain and support ICT infrastructure across all Plan International Jordan locations, including field offices and camps, ensuring reliable network connectivity, system availability, and technical support.
- Conduct ICT infrastructure assessments for new offices, premises, and field locations, identifying connectivity, hardware, network, security, and system integration requirements to ensure operational readiness before staff deployment.

2\. Helpdesk and End-User Technical Support

- Manage and maintain an effective ICT helpdesk support process, ensuring that user requests, incidents, and technical issues are properly recorded, monitored, prioritized, and resolved.
- Provide first- and second-line technical support to employees and beneficiaries, where applicable, through onsite, remote, telephone, and other approved support channels.
- Install, configure, maintain, upgrade, and troubleshoot desktops, laptops, printers, scanners, mobile devices, and other ICT equipment.
- Diagnose and resolve hardware, software, operating system, network connectivity, email, login, user profile, and access permission issues.
- Provide support for Microsoft Windows operating systems, Microsoft Office applications, email clients, and other organizational software.
- Perform software installations, system configurations, hardware upgrades, operating system updates, and troubleshooting in accordance with organizational ICT standards.
- Coordinate laptop and equipment preparation, configuration, allocation, and delivery for new employees.
- Provide technical guidance and awareness sessions to employees on ICT systems, applications, cybersecurity, and appropriate technology usage.
- Maintain records of ICT incidents, support requests, troubleshooting activities, and recurring technical issues to identify improvement opportunities.

3.Cybersecurity, Backup and Business Continuity

- Implement and monitor ICT security measures, including firewalls, VPNs, endpoint protection, access controls, MFA, and security updates.
- Administer backup, storage, and recovery solutions, ensuring data integrity, availability, and business continuity.
- Monitor security alerts, vulnerabilities, and backup logs, and coordinate incident response and corrective actions.
- Support phishing awareness campaigns, security testing, and employee cybersecurity awareness initiatives.
- Document security incidents, vulnerabilities, corrective actions, and mitigation measures.
- Coordinate with regional and global ICT security teams to address security incidents, implement security requirements, and ensure compliance with organizational standards.
- Maintain backup schedules, recovery procedures, and disaster recovery documentation.

4.Microsoft 365, Cloud Services and Document Management

- Administer Microsoft 365 services, including Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams, SharePoint Online, OneDrive, and related cloud applications.
- Manage user accounts, licenses, shared mailboxes, distribution groups, security groups, permissions, and email services.
- Administer SharePoint sites, document libraries, access permissions, and departmental file structures.
- Support digital document archiving, file migration, and SharePoint–OneDrive integration to improve document accessibility and promote paperless workflows.
- Manage and support Google Workspace, organizational domains, DNS records, hosting, and related digital platforms.
- Provide technical guidance and user support on Microsoft 365 applications, cloud services, and collaboration tools.

5\. ICT Projects, Digital Transformation and Strategic Planning

- Contribute to the development and implementation of annual ICT work plans, technology roadmaps, and initiatives aligned with organizational objectives and operational requirements.
- Plan and support ICT infrastructure upgrades, system migrations, technology deployments, and digital transformation projects.
- Coordinate the implementation, testing, and verification of new systems, Microsoft 365 services, data migrations, and other approved technology solutions while minimizing operational disruptions.
- Identify opportunities to improve ICT services, automate manual processes, enhance cybersecurity, and increase operational efficiency through appropriate digital solutions.
- Evaluate and test new technologies, applications, and equipment to ensure compatibility, security, and suitability before implementation.
- Provide technical advice and recommendations to management on ICT infrastructure, technology investments, system improvements, and operational risks.
- Coordinate with internal departments, regional and global ICT teams, and external service providers to ensure the successful implementation of ICT projects.
- Prepare periodic ICT reports covering infrastructure performance, service delivery, security, asset management, ongoing projects, and technology requirements.
- Provide technical training, guidance, and knowledge-sharing sessions to employees and ensure proper handover of ICT projects, systems, documentation, and ongoing activities

6\. ICT Procurement, Vendor Management and Documentation

- Provide technical input into ICT procurement processes, including preparing technical specifications, evaluating technical proposals, and recommending suitable hardware, software, and services.
- Coordinate with procurement and finance departments, vendors, suppliers, internet service providers, and maintenance companies to ensure the effective delivery and maintenance of ICT services and equipment.
- Follow up on service requests, warranties, software licenses, subscriptions, maintenance agreements, and service contracts.
- Verify the delivery, installation, configuration, and acceptance of ICT equipment and services against approved technical specifications.
- Maintain and regularly update ICT documentation, including network diagrams, server configurations, system inventories, asset records, user access records, and infrastructure documentation.
- Develop and maintain Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) covering user onboarding and offboarding, account management, equipment allocation, software installation, backups, recovery, and incident reporting.
