title: VA26P184V01 MRC Coordinator (M3)
source: International Centre for Migration Policy Development
body:
MRAPP funded by the Government of the Netherlands, aims to strengthen migration prevention efforts and improve access to migration-related information, counselling, referral and reintegration services in Iraq. The project is implemented by ICMPD in close coordination with the Ministry of Migration and Displacement and other relevant governmental and local stakeholders, with a focus on strengthening and expanding the Migrant Resource Centre (MRC) model.

The position will be based within the MRAPP project team and will report to the Project Manager, while working closely with relevant ICMPD colleagues, MRC staff, government counterparts and project stakeholders to support the effective delivery of project activities and results.

## Functional Overview

Working closely with the respective project manager, the Migrant Resource Centre (MRC) Coordinator based on solid knowledge and experience, supports the technical and administrative functions, coordination, and management of the MRC in a designated duty station, ensuring the effective and efficient coordination and operation of the MRC, in accordance with ICMPD rules and procedures. They ensure effective communication, information and service delivery and contribute to the organisation of events and activities organised by the MRC. They work collaboratively with the MRC Senior Counsellors, Counsellors, administrative support staff, project teams, relevant local counterparts, and Units at ICMPD Headquarters, ensuring the effective and timely delivery of MRC activities and services.

## Key Results

***MRC Coordination:*** The MRC workplan activities timely and effectively implemented with substantive assistance being provided to the respective project manager to facilitate effective information and service delivery on safe, regular, and orderly migration, including return and reintegration. The work of the MRC Senior Counsellors, Counsellors and MRC activities, progress and expenditures regularly monitored with feedback provided to the project implementation team. The respective project manager ably supported in the provision of all communication and correspondence concerning the MRC, including participation in MRC activities with government, national and internal organisations, academia, and other MRC stakeholders. The MRC database maintained and accurately updated, ensuring the timely and accurate entry of data for each MRC client, outreach activities and coordination meetings, completion of client forms, meeting minutes and session evaluations. Oversight and security of all data-related materials regularly monitored and overseen with any potential vulnerabilities to data storage and/or data devices being regularly monitored, ensuring data protection and compliance with GDPR.

***Stakeholder Management:*** The project manager effectively supported with the establishment of good cooperation and partnership with national and local government, technical and vocational training institutes, academia, faith-based groups, community leaders, organizations operating in the areas of resettlement and humanitarian admission and anti-trafficking and smuggling networks, media, and other local partners and organisations to conduct outreach sessions and community education. Opportunities proactively identified for partnerships that contribute to the overall goals of the MRC.

***MRC Operational Activities:*** Efficient customer service provided to the MRC clients via the MRC hotline or helpline numbers, email, live chat, and social media accounts. Relevant information and communication materials disseminated to a variety of clients visiting and attending MRC sessions, including initiating, and following up on referrals, and linking them with partners and service providers such as government agencies, technical and vocational institutes, CSOs and private sector. Respective processes and forms regarding pre-migration and pre-employment formalities for intending migrants and their families, and pre-departure (as well as post-arrival, if applicable) orientation briefings to outgoing and returning migrants efficiently implemented.

***Support to Information, Training and Further Development Activities:*** Effective contributions provided to the organisation and monitoring of pre-departure (as well as post-arrival, if applicable) orientation sessions and training, community events, orientation sessions, media outreach, and engage with the relevant authorities managing the sessions and events. Training targeting representatives of the government, media and civilsociety ably implemented through coordination, content development, delivery, and reporting. Inputs provided to the development of new flyers, fact sheets, country-specific migration profiles and other MRC information, education and communication materials with the MRC website, Facebook page and other social media accounts being regularly updated. Maintain financial files and records according to ICMPD procedures.

***MRC Administrative Activities:*** In consultation with the project manager and project team members, the timely preparation and submission ensured of weekly, biweekly, monthly quarterly and annual progress reports, work plans and budget, meeting agendas and minutes, activity and mission reports, expenditure plans and advance budget requests Assistance provided to the timely procurement of equipment, materials and services required for outreach activities, events, and missions.

## Required Expertise

- ​Solid organizational, planning, coordination and prioritizing skills and abilities.
- Upon consultation with the supervisor, the ability to make decisions in full compliance with ICMPD’s operational regulations and rules.
- Analytical thinking to gather, analyse and compile information, identifying critical relationships and patterns among data and proposing workable solutions.
- Understanding of migration dynamics in the country.
- High sense of initiative and good judgement to be able to work independently with minimum supervision.
- Strong sense of client orientation and good understanding of effective service delivery, community engagement, outreach, and social work.
- Ability to work effectively with people of different nationalities and cultural backgrounds.
- Capability to establish effective relationships across the organisation at all levels.

### Qualifications, Experience and Language Skills

- Master’s degree related to the area of work. A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree or equivalent) with two additional years of relevant work experience may be accepted in lieu of the master’s degree.
- Minimum of 6 years of position-specific experience.
- Working experience with international organisations is an asset.
- Experience in coordination, management, and office administration.
- Experience in working with local authorities and businesses.
- Experience in migration in the country.
- Solid organisational skills.
- Proficiency in English and Arabic (verbal/written) is required.
- Proficiency in the use of standard IT tools.

title: VA26P187V01 Project Manager (IP3)
source: International Centre for Migration Policy Development
body:
## Functional Overview

The Project Manager is responsible for the direction, management, coordination, implementation, control and completion of project(s) and the management of project team(s) while remaining aligned with the strategy, goals, regulatory framework, standard administrative practices and operating procedures of ICMPD and with partner and donor agreements. They actively contribute to project and capacity development and resource mobilisation efforts.

## Key Results

***Project Cycle Management:*** In collaboration with all relevant stakeholders, project plans, scope, objectives and budget(s) effectively determined and developed, ensuring resource availability and technical expertise allocation. Milestones developed to track progress and manage any changes in project scope, schedule and costs. Quality standards determined to ensure the quality level of the project(s). Risks effectively identified and analysed. Project performance tools developed and regularly measured using appropriate techniques. Project and donor reporting accurately drafted and delivered in a timely manner.

***Project Resources Management:*** The type, quantity and quality of resources required to achieve the project’s goals accurately identified during the project planning phase together with the respective internal partners and within the project(s) budget(s). The project team(s) skills sets, roles and responsibilities clearly defined. Contracts effectively negotiated between subcontractors, consultants, or service providers, ensuring a transparent competitive basis in line with ICMPD’s rules, regulations and procedures.

***Stakeholder Management:*** Stakeholder expectations and working relationships effectively managed and communication regularly undertaken to ensure all stakeholders are kept informed. Project updates created and circulated to stakeholders and the project team(s).

***Project Team Management:*** Project team(s) knowledge base developed, ensuring the project(s) benefit from the right knowledge, experience, and skills sets and that team members are committed to the goals of the project(s). Project team(s) effectively motivated and mentored to ensure the highest quality project deliverables. Evaluation of the performance of project team(s), experts, consultants and service providers regularly and systematically undertaken in accordance with ICMPD´s performance management procedures.

***Project Development and Resource Mobilisation:*** Substantive input provided to the design of projects and to portfolios that support the achievement of capacity development goals and sustainable approaches. Resource mobilization activities initiated and proposals developed for projects requiring additional funding, with funding options identified.

## Required Expertise

- ​Ability to effectively manage projects and project teams in an international context.
- Proven capability to promote capacity development measures across the full project cycle management.
- Analytical thinking and ability to integrate new approaches and innovations to ensure the effective implementation of projects.
- Familiarity with monitoring, evaluation and learning tools for tracking progress toward results and documenting project/programme achievements.
- Demonstrated success in building networks and partnerships and in the initiation and deployment of knowledge management and resource mobilisation activities.

## Qualifications, Experience and Language Skills

- ​Master’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field. A first-level university degree (Bachelor’s degree or equivalent) with two additional years of relevant work experience may be accepted in lieu of the Master’s degree.
- Minimum of 5 years of experience in the development and management of projects and project teams in the field of migration or a relevant related field, at the international level.
- Solid drafting, communication and presentation skills.
- Proficiency in (verbal/written) English, proficiency in the language of the duty station is an asset.
- Proficiency in the use of standard IT tools.

body:

- Good organisational, drafting and communication skills.
- Proficiency in (verbal/written) English and French is required, proficiency in Arabic, particularly Tunisian Arabic is an asset.
- Proficiency in the use of standard IT tools.

title: VA26P069V03 MRC Counsellor (M1)
source: International Centre for Migration Policy Development
body:
> *Note: Please note that this vacancy has been republished. Applicants who have already submitted an application do not need to reapply.*

The overall objective of the PROTECT project is to contribute to migrant protection in the target countries covering all phases of (in and out) migration, including countering and preventing irregular migration, trafficking in human beings and smuggling of migrants. An MRC has been opened within this project. The purpose of the project is to contribute to strengthening of the MRC work and to ensuring their long term sustainability after the project. ​

## Functional Overview

Reporting to the Project Manager, based at the ICMPD Headquarters in Vienna, and working closely with the respective Migration Resource Centre (MRC) Coordinator, the MRC Counsellor assists with the implementation of MRC activities and workplans, in support of effective communication, information and service delivery. They contribute to the organisation of events and outreach activities organised by the MRC. They work collaboratively with the MRC Coordinator and other Counsellors, administrative support staff, project teams, relevant local counterparts, and Units at Headquarters, ensuring the effective and timely delivery of MRC activities and services, in accordance with ICMPD rules and procedures.

## Key Results

***Support to MRC Activities:*** Via various means and platforms such as face-to-face, phone and online, counselling, guidance, referral and information provided to a variety of clients (prospective or returning migrants, migrants, families of migrants, etc.) who visit or attend MRC activities, initiating and following up on referrals, linking them with relevant agencies depending on their needs, e.g. technical and vocational institutes to upgrade their skills or with the relevant authorities for the processing of their documents for overseas employment. Outreach activities supported via the use of media and social media and participation in online discussions, forums or symposiums, conferences, and other related events. In collaboration with the MRC Coordinator the MRC website and database, Facebook page and other social media accounts regularly updated.

***Support to Outreach Activities:*** In cooperation with relevant agencies both in the public and private sector, networks and contacts effectively established. Community events and outreach activities organised such as briefings in academic and training institutions, symposia with civil society, training of education or emigration consultancies, and the setting-up of booths, kiosks, or similar structures in public places to disseminate information and materials on safe, orderly, and regular migration, including on return and reintegration.

***Preparation of Information Materials:*** In collaboration with the ICMPD team and whenever applicable, with consultants or experts, research or mapping undertaken of available migration-related programmes, services, and activities of various stakeholders. Knowledge materials compiled on migration that are helpful in the full operation and functioning of the MRC. Additional knowledge products and information materials revised, prepared, or further developed, as necessary, such as brochures, handbooks, audio-visual products, web-based information documents, etc. Online discussions relevant to migration, regularly maintained and populated, initiating regular and timely responses to issues raised and information requested.

***Support to the MRC Coordination Activities:*** Assistance provided to the respective MRC Coordinator to ensure the timely, efficient, and effective implementation of MRC activities, and with the monitoring and updating of the workplans, as necessary, ensuring that outputs and outcomes are aligned and integrated with the national priorities and strategies of government partners, and of the projects. Substantive contributions provided to the preparation of relevant reports, responses to client feedback and monitoring and reporting to relevant agencies on any policy or programmatic recommendations. Information materials compiled and prepared for dissemination. The MRC database regularly updated recording relevant activities, events and outreach activities undertaken. Effective support provided to the MRC Coordinator in preparing weekly, quarterly and annual progress reports, work plans and budget, meeting agendas and minutes, activity and mission reports, expenditure plans and advance budget requests on agreed formats, and other documentary requirements.

## Required Expertise

- ​Solid organizational, planning and prioritizing skills and abilities.
- Upon consultation with the supervisor, ability to make decisions in full compliance with ICMPD’s operational regulations and rules.
- Analytical thinking to gather, analyse and compile information, identifying critical relationships and patterns among data and proposing workable solutions.
- An understanding of migration dynamics in the country.
- Experience in the area of migration in the country.
- High sense of initiative and good judgement to be able to work independently with minimum supervision.
- Strong sense of client orientation and good understanding of effective service delivery, community engagement, outreach, and social work.
- Ability to work effectively with people of different nationalities and cultural backgrounds.
- Capability to establish effective relationships across the organisation at all levels.

## Qualifications, Experience and Language Skills

- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in a relevant field. High school diploma or equivalent with two additional years of relevant work experience may be accepted in lieu of the Bachelor’s degree.
- Minimum of 2 years of position-specific experience.
- Working experience with international organisations, is an asset.
- Experience in office administration and management.
- Experience in working with local authorities and businesses.
- Solid organisational skills.
- Proficiency in English and Uzbek language (verbal/written) is required, proficiency in Russian language is an asset. ​​
- Proficiency in the use of standard IT tools.

title: Operations Manager
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
## About Refugee-Led Research Hub (RLRH)

The Refugee-Led Research Hub (RLRH) supports individuals with lived experience of displacement to become leaders in fields related to human rights, forced migration, humanitarian response and development, politics, and law, among other areas. We do so by delivering academic and professional development programming to a global cohort of students who have been affected by displacement—as refugees, asylum seekers, IDPs, stateless, and beyond—supporting access to graduate degrees and advanced career opportunities. RLRH also creates opportunities for researchers with displacement backgrounds to lead primary and secondary research studies, from start to finish.

RLRH’s team is composed of colleagues who are deeply committed to advancing refugee leadership, the majority of whom have lived experience of displacement. Our network of staff, researchers, students, and other affiliates is made up of 1,400+ individuals across 80+ countries. RLRH has five active offices: our first was established in Nairobi in 2020, we have had an office at the University of Oxford since 2021, and we have since developed physical hubs in Kakuma refugee camp (Kenya), Kuala Lumpur (Malaysia), Kampala (Uganda), and in the Oxfordshire community (UK).

From October 2025 RLRH is funded to serve as a technical partner for the Mastercard Foundation’s Scholars Program network, advancing an ambitious global agenda to support displacement-affected learners to access 1,000+ graduate-level scholarships at partner universities around the world. RLRH provides expert guidance and implements specialised programmes to help these learners enter university, thrive on course, and pursue meaningful and enduring careers on completion of their degrees. A complementary, refugee-led research agenda designed by RLRH colleagues produces insights to help Scholars Program partner universities and other stakeholders accelerate positive, long-lasting systems change.

## Job Description

### About the Operations and Strategy Pillar

The Operations and Strategy Pillar provides the organisational infrastructure that enables RLRH to deliver high-quality programmes and advance its mission at scale. Working across finance, operations, people, organisational systems, planning, governance, and institutional partnerships, the Pillar ensures colleagues have the support and systems required to deliver meaningful work across multiple countries, institutional contexts, and funding streams.

As a globally distributed organisation operating across the University of Oxford, the British Institute in Eastern Africa (BIEA), and a growing network of international offices, RLRH works within a complex operating environment that requires careful coordination, strong financial stewardship, and adaptable ways of working. The Operations and Strategy Pillar helps bring these different contexts together, building consistent organisational approaches while responding to local operational needs.

Beyond supporting day-to-day operations, the Pillar plays a central role in shaping how RLRH works and develops as an organisation. Through the continuous improvement of policies, systems, and ways of working that strengthen organisational effectiveness, improve organisational decision-making, support compliance, and enables the organisation to respond to new opportunities and challenges

RLRH is entering a significant period of growth, with new regional hubs, expanding programmes, and a diversifying portfolio of funding and institutional partnerships. The Operations and Strategy Pillar helps turn this ambition into reality, building the foundations for sustainable growth while ensuring RLRH remains resilient, effective , and true to its mission.

### Overview of the Role

As RLRH continues to expand globally, the Operations Manager will report to and work in close partnership with the Director of Operations and Strategy to provide operational leadership across the organisation's finance and operational support functions, ensuring systems, processes, and resources effectively enable the delivery of RLRH's programmes.

As an organisation hosted by the University of Oxford and operating through international host institutions, RLRH works within established finance and grants management structures rather than operating as an independent finance function. The Operations Manager will also work closely with the Oxford Department of International Development (ODID) finance team, Research Support, Post-Award, and other professional services across the University of Oxford, as well as colleagues within partner host institutions such as BIEA in Kenya and Ideas Academy in Malaysia. While these partnered teams provide institutional operations and financial administration oversight, this role is responsible for coordinating RLRH’s internal financial planning, operations management, grant oversight, and organisational systems, ensuring financial and operational processes effectively support programme delivery, organisational priorities, sustainable growth, and compliance with institutional and donor requirements.

The role has responsibility for providing line management to the Finance Officer and Administrative Assistant based at the University of Oxford. The postholder will oversee finance, administration, procurement, travel, contracts, and operational support activities, ensuring these services operate efficiently,and maintain compliance,

Success in the role will depend not only on strong technical and operational expertise, but also on the ability to navigate complex institutional environments, build trusted relationships, and ensure colleagues have the systems, guidance and operational support they need to deliver RLRH's programmes and mission successfully.

### Responsibilities

**Financial Systems, Analysis, and Reporting (25%)**

- Lead the preparation of regular financial reports and analyses to support organisational decision-making by providing RLRH senior leadership with clear oversight of financial performance, available resources, grant expenditure, financial risks, and opportunities.
- Coordinate the preparation, consolidation, and review of project budgets, financial forecasts, and expenditure reports across multiple funding streams.
- Maintain oversight over organisational financial commitments and advise on financial viability of new contracts and supplier agreements based on available and eligible grant balances.
- Manage cashflow forecasting and liquidity, ensuring RLRH can meet its ambitious global commitments and calling attention to fundraising risks.
- Lead the continuous development and improvement of financial systems, reporting tools, and workflows, ensuring information from host institutions and accounting systems is integrated effectively to support accurate financial management and reporting.

**Financial Controls and Expenditure Tracking (20%)**

- Provide oversight and quality assurance to the RLRH Finance Officer to ensure transaction-level tagging is accurate.
- Establish, implement, and monitor financial standards for how RLRH tracks expenses, ensuring alignment with Oxford, BIEA, and other emergent institutional compliance requirements.
- Coordinate and support internal and external audits, ensuring appropriate records, documentation, and controls are maintained.
- Build effective working relationships with host institutions to ensure compliance with responsibilities set out in collaboration agreements and financial reporting requirements.
- Work closely with the RLRH Finance Officer and Departmental Finance team to ensure month-end financial transactions, including journals and cost transfers, are completed accurately and in a timely manner, with expenditure correctly allocated to the appropriate funding streams, projects and cost centres.

**Operational Policy, Governance, and Training (15%)**

- Lead the development, implementation, and improvement of RLRH-specific financial and operational policies, SOPs, and guidance within the frameworks established by host institutions. Work with relevant institutional teams to ensure RLRH procedures complement and consistently apply wider organisational processes, while also meeting donor requirements and responding to RLRH's operational needs.
- Strengthen financial capability across RLRH by providing training and guidance on budgeting, monitoring, expenditure, and financial procedures.
- Identify and implement opportunities to improve operational processes, reduce administrative burden, and embed scalable ways of working across RLRH.

**Donor Management and Compliance (15%)**

- Lead the preparation of budgets and financial information for funding proposals, renewals, and organisational growth initiatives, working closely with senior leadership, programme teams, and host institutions.
- Maintain detailed knowledge of donor budgets and expenditure restrictions ensuring organisational spending remains compliant with approved budgets and funder requirements.
- Support the development of collaboration agreements and MOUs with host institutions and programme partners, ensuring appropriate financial and operational arrangements are in place for programme delivery.
- Act as the principal operations and finance liaison for funders working closely with the University Post-Award focal point to coordinate financial reporting, budget amendments, funder approvals, and other grant management requirements.
- Review donor financial reports prepared by the Finance Officer and lead re-budgeting exercises as per organisational priorities and donor requirements and deadlines (e.g. quarterly, bi-annually, annually).
- Provide strategic financial advice and guidance to programme teams on budgeting, expenditure, donor requirements and financial planning throughout the grant lifecycle.

**Organisational Planning and Budgeting (15%)**

- Lead the delivery of RLRH’s annual budgeting and budget revisions, working closely with the Director of Operations and Strategy, senior leadership and the MEL team.
- Develop and maintain a multi-dimensional budgeting framework that supports organisational planning, resource allocation and budget management across departments, donors, programmes, and cost categories.
- Work closely with the Department Finance Manager to coordinate the quarterly forecasting process, reviewing financial performance against budget, and updating forecasts.
- Work closely with senior leadership and programme leads to ensure organisational planning is rooted in financial reality and that data collection informs future budget allocations.

**People Management and Team Support (10%)**

- Provide day-today leadership, coaching, workload planning, and quality assurance to the Finance Officer and Administrative Assistant, fostering their professional growth and technical proficiency.
- Maintain a dotted-line relationship with the East Africa Operations Coordinator, the SEA Programme Manager, and other future hubs to ensure regional financial workflows support global RLRH standards.

### **Selection criteria**

**Essential**

- Educated to a degree-level in finance, accounting, business, economics, or a related subject, or equivalent relevant professional experience.
- Significant professional experience in finance and/or operations within the charity sector, higher education, international development, research or another complex multi-stakeholder environment.
- Experience developing, improving or overseeing financial systems, processes and reporting tools, including working with multiple financial platforms and institutional stakeholders.
- Strong analytical skills and advanced proficiency in spreadsheets and financial data analysis, with the ability to interpret and communicate complex financial information effectively.
- Expertise in complex multi-dimensional budgeting (by donor/programme) and managing the financial complexities of large-scale grants (e.g., Mastercard Foundation).
- Proven ability to set standards, audit regional teams, and develop SOPs that balance rigor with the needs of international development contexts.
- Proven experience managing donor-funded grants and ensuring compliance with funder requirements.
- Experience leading, managing, and developing finance/administrative staff in a high-growth environment.
- Experience preparing and reviewing grant budgets, supporting funding proposals, and contributing to donor financial reporting processes.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to manage up to executive leadership and liaise effectively with University administrators.
- Experience using a range of digital systems to support finance and operations, including accounting software, budgeting and reporting tools, collaboration platforms (e.g. Slack), HR, or CRM systems.
- Experience working across teams, organisations, and institutional environments and managing competing requirements and priorities.
- Demonstrated commitment to working inclusively and effectively within diverse, multicultural, and international teams.

**Desirable**

- Familiarity with University of Oxford financial procedures and higher education administration.
- Experience working in financial operations in Low and Middle Income Countries (LMIC), East Africa, and/or with fiscal sponsors like the BIEA.
- Professional accounting qualification (e.g., ACCA, CIMA) or equivalent.
- Knowledge of international development, higher education, research, migration, refugee studies, or related sectors.
- Fluency in another language spoken by RLRH learners and affiliates, for example, Arabic, Farsi, French, or Swahili.

title: IDC Operations Manager
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
body:
**Reports To:** Executive Director  
**Status:** FTE 0.8 - 4 days per week  
**Direct Reports: ●** Finance Coordinator  
● Administration Coordinator  
● Grants and Finance Officer  
**Location:** Remote working, based in **Australia**, **Germany**, **the Netherlands**, or **the United Kingdom**.  
*You must have the right to work in the country for which you apply. IDC is unable to support work visa applications or relocation.*  
**Languages:** Fluency and excellent communication skills in oral and written English  
**Compensation:** Per annum depending on skills and experience:  
**Australia -** SCHADS Level 6, pro rata for 0.8 FTE  
**The Netherlands, Germany, UK -** 48,000-56,000 EUR gross annually for 0.8 FTE (based on a full-time equivalent of 60,000-70,000 EUR)

**Background**

[International Detention Coalition (IDC)](https://idcoalition.org/) is a unique global network of over 200 civil society organisations and individuals in more than 75 countries, which coordinates with members and partners on advocacy, research, coalition and capacity building, to eliminate immigration detention and advance rights-based alternatives to detention. IDC is a highly recognised, impact-driven organisation, offering a stimulating workplace committed to local, national, regional and global change.

**Role Purpose**

The Operations Manager is responsible for making sure the organisation has the financial, legal, human resources (HR) systems, and operational infrastructure needed to function effectively, and sustainably, including risk management and ensuring compliance in the countries where IDC operates.

**Role Summary**

The Operations Manager provides strategic leadership for the organisation's financial, legal, HR systems, and operational infrastructure, ensuring that the organisation has the systems, capacity and controls required to operate effectively, sustainably and compliantly in multi-currency and multi-country settings.

The role sets the frameworks, standards and priorities through which operational functions are delivered, providing oversight of the Finance Coordinator, Administration Coordinator and Grants and Finance Officer, as well as relevant external providers. The Operations Manager focuses on organisational systems, planning, risk, quality and improvement.

The role is responsible for strengthening the organisation's operational infrastructure as it develops, ensuring that systems are fit for purpose, risks are identified and appropriately managed, legal and regulatory obligations are met, and personnel have the systems and support they need to work effectively.

The Operations Manager reports to the Executive Director (ED) and works closely with the Programmes Manager, Finance and Administration personnel, Regional Managers, and relevant service providers. The Operations Manager forms part of the Senior Management Team.

**Role Responsibilities**

**Finance and Organisational Sustainability**

- Provide strategic oversight of financial management, grants financial management, budgeting, forecasting and organisational finances.
- Oversee and support the Finance Coordinator and Grants and Finance Officer, ensuring effective implementation of finance and grants systems.
- Work closely with the ED, Programmes Manager, finance and admin team, and relevant managers on annual budgeting and financial planning.
- Ensure effective monitoring of financial performance, cash flow, expenditure and financial risks, providing advice to the ED and Senior Management Team.
- Oversee the establishment and management of appropriate financial controls, payrolls systems, approval processes and delegations.
- Oversee relationships with accountants, auditors, tax advisers and other financial service providers.
- Lead on the improvements to financial systems as the organisation develops or operates in new places.
- Oversee budgeting systems and allocations ensuring accurate compliance of grants finance and audit requirements.
- Work closely with the Finance Coordinator and oversee the annual audit processes for IDC and other related programme audits.
- Ensure financial systems provide accurate and timely information for informed organisational decision-making.

**Human Resources Systems**

- Support the Executive Director to implement the organisation's human resources systems, ensuring personnel structures and capabilities are aligned with organisational priorities and needs.
- Develop and implement recruitment and planning strategies and systems, including approaches to attracting, retaining and developing personnel across different regions and jurisdictions.
- Develop appropriate and coherent benchmarks and frameworks for personnel roles that are localised, including remuneration, benefits and capacity, and use these to inform organisational planning, monitoring and recruitment.
- Oversee and manage human resources systems, including employment arrangements in different jurisdictions, benefits, onboarding, performance management and other HR related systems.
- Ensure human resources practices are compliant with applicable local legislation and organisational policies.
- Support the enhancement of a wellbeing culture at IDC with related systems and benefits.
- Oversee and support the Administration Coordinator's implementation of HR processes, ensuring systems are consistent, effective and fit for purpose.

**Risk, Compliance and Contracts**

- Work closely with the ED to coordinate the organisational risk management framework, including the development, monitoring and mitigation of key organisational risks.
- Manage and provide oversight of the organisation's legal entities and ensure statutory, regulatory and governance obligations are met as needed.
- Establish and maintain appropriate internal controls across financial, operational, HR, data and compliance functions.
- Oversee the organisation's grant finance compliance infrastructure, working closely with the ED, Programmes Manager and Grants and Finance Officer.
- Ensure systems are in place to monitor donor financial and administrative requirements, contractual obligations, reporting deadlines and compliance risks.
- Oversee organisational contracts and agreements, ensuring appropriate systems for review, approval, documentation and record-keeping.
- Coordinate legal, tax and compliance advice where required.
- Ensure appropriate continuity, sustainability and contingency planning is in place.

**Policies, Systems and Administration**

- Lead the development, review and implementation of organisational policies, procedures and operational frameworks, liaising with the Executive Director.
- Ensure organisational processes, approval pathways and delegated authorities are clear, proportionate and consistently applied.
- Provide strategic oversight of IT, cybersecurity, data protection and digital infrastructure.
- Ensure appropriate systems, security arrangements and technology standards are in place for a global remote organisation.
- Oversee organisational procurement frameworks and controls.
- Provide oversight and support to the Administration Coordinator, ensuring administrative systems are efficient and responsive to organisational needs.
- Identify opportunities to streamline processes, improve systems and reduce unnecessary administrative burden.

**Organisational Development & Operational Improvement**

- Lead the ongoing development of the organisation's operational infrastructure and systems, as its size, funding and geographic reach evolve.
- Regularly and proactively assess organisational systems, platforms, capacity and processes to identify gaps, risks and opportunities for improvement.
- Develop practical frameworks and standards to strengthen organisational effectiveness, accountability and resilience.
- Lead operational improvement and organisational development initiatives and monitor their implementation.
- Identify emerging organisational needs and advise the ED on appropriate systems, structures and resourcing.
- Any other relevant tasks agreed with the Executive Director.

**Core Responsibilities**

- Actively contribute to a culture of agile learning, collaboration, teamwork and support within IDC’s team.
- Demonstrate passion and alignment with IDC’s mission, vision and core values of innovation, collaboration, respect, inclusion, representation and being solutions-focused.

- Demonstrated experience managing and supporting personnel responsible for finance, HR, administration or other operational functions.
- Strong understanding of organisational financial management, including budgeting, forecasting, financial controls and financial risk.
- Experience overseeing HR and employment processes, ideally across multiple jurisdictions or employment arrangements.
- Experience managing organisational compliance and/or legal or regulatory requirements.
- Demonstrated ability to develop, implement and improve organisational systems, policies and processes.
- Experience working in a geographically distributed or remote organisation or demonstrated ability to manage operational functions across locations.
- Strong judgement, problem-solving and prioritisation skills, with the ability to balance strategic priorities with responsive day-to-day operational needs.
- A high level of flexibility and adaptability, including the ability to work well and collaboratively with others.
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to communicate clearly and practically regarding complex matters.

title: General coordinator (head of mission) (F/M) - Pakistan
body:
For more than 40 years, Médecins du Monde (MdM), a campaigning medical organisation committed to international solidarity, has been caring for the most vulnerable populations here and abroad. It has continued to bear witness to obstacles that exist in accessing healthcare and has secured sustainable improvements in health-for-all policies.

Those working for this independent organisation do not solely dispense care and treatment but condemn violations of human dignity and rights and fight to improve matters for populations living in precarious situations.

MdM France currently works in 30 countries across all continents to facilitate access to healthcare through 6 political battles:

- Sexual and Reproductive Health Rights
- Migration, Exile, Human Rights and Health
- Harm Reduction
- Environment and Health
- Humanitarian Space
- Healthcare systems and rights

**MdM in Pakistan**

MdM France has been operating in Pakistan since 1996, mainly in Punjab and KPK provinces. In Punjab, over the past 30 years, MdM has been implementing Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) including family planning and gender based violence projects. Present since 2009 in KP, MdM has been working with the Afghan refugees and internally displaced persons providing essential primary healthcare services including mental health and psychological support. In KP, across the course of the years, we have covered many districts and have built strong acceptance among the local communities and authorities. We have also responded to multiples emergencies including the 2022 and 2025 floods.

For the 2027–2029 period, MdM will continue to focus on advancing on SRHR as the central pillar of all programming in Pakistan. All interventions will be firmly grounded in a comprehensive, integrated, and rights-based SRHR strategy with particular focus on access to family planning services and cervical cancer awareness and screening. Developing specific initiatives focused on cervical cancer would be critical to the mission. Additionally, MdM is monitoring the situation related to humanitarian needs of Afghan refugees in KP and will intend to develop new actions to ensure humanitarian assistance to the most vulnerable.

Currently the mission has a portfolio of around 500K€/year, with 20 staffs and 2 offices (coordination in Islamabad and one field office in Mardan/KP). A variety of institutional donors used to support the mission, but the funding environment is currently shrinking, and MdM is covering the mission with core funds. One of the main stakes of 2027 will be to secure new institutional fundings and ensure sustainability of MdM in the country.

**About the role**

As general coordinator, you will supervise the proper implementation of MdM strategy and operations in the country.

One of your main responsibilities is to drive a strategic restructuring of the Pakistan mission, ensuring the transition to a strengthened and autonomous national team.

**What you’ll do**

Under the supervision of the desk manager, you are responsible for the overall management of the Pakistan mission.

Your main responsibilities are the following:

- Recruit, manage, train and motivate the mission’s team
- Define the operational and advocacy strategy together with the coordination team, the desk manager and the volunteer board delegates of the mission
- Plan and monitor activities, implement corrective action when necessary, providing technical support to the team
- Represent MdM with authorities, local actors, partners, donors and the media
- Monitor partnership agreements with partners, authorities and donors, seek out and develop new partnerships, and ensure or supervise fundraising
- Ensure the financial coverage of the mission by leading fundraising and budget management
- Draft, adapt and monitor safety regulations and procedures and coordinate crisis management in the region
- Implement and monitor the application of MdM’s programmatic and support services framework, policies and procedures
- Supervise reporting to MdM and donors

**Who you’ll work with**

You will report directly to the Desk Manager based at HQ.

As General Coordinator, you will be the head of the country coordination team and you will manage directly a team composed of: Deputy Coordinator programs, Deputy Coordinator in charge of support services, Medical Advisor, Humanitarian Access and Risks Advisor and Field Coordinator/KP.

## REQUIREMENTS

**You are the right match if you:**

- Have 5+ years' experience in the humanitarian sector, including coordination and expatriate roles
- Have led teams and operations in complex or insecure environments
- Are confident representing an organisation with donors, authorities and humanitarian actors
- Can negotiate effectively, manage risks and oversee security matters
- Bring strong strategic thinking and sound operational judgment
- Have experience with programme, budget and support function management, ideally in health and SRHR
- Enjoy coaching teams, building capacity and developing talent
- Communicate with diplomacy, adapt quickly and lead through uncertainty
- Are comfortable with Microsoft Office and mapping tools
- Are fluent in English

**This role may not suit you if you...**

- Prefer stable environments with limited operational or security challenges
- Are uncomfortable making difficult decisions, negotiating or representing an organisation externally
- Prefer specialist or technical roles over broad leadership and management responsibilities
- Are not aligned with MdM’s values

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info: https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/  
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

**Ready to apply?**

We only need your CV and a cover letter.  
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

## **EMPLOYMENT CONDITIONS**

Contract & status:

- Gross monthly salary: 3 664 €
- Fixed-term contract of 6 months starting on January 2027
- Single posting

Work environment:

- Position based in Islamabad with frequent travels to field locations (office in Mardan/KP)

Benefits:

- 13th month salary (paid in 2 installments after 6 months of service)
- Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Individual guesthouse
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility

Essentials:

- 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
- Strong commitment to inclusion and fighting all forms of discrimination
- More info: https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/

**Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.  
If you are officially recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know.

title: Monitoring Officer - Roster
body:
**Monitoring Officer - Roster**

**Summary**

**Languages:** One of 12 roster languages (Pashto, Dari, Levantine Arabic, Sudanese Arabic, Bengali, Egyptian Arabic, Urdu, Moroccan Darija, Iraqi Arabic, Kurdish Sorani, Kurdish Badini and Somali), plus English and/or Arabic and/or French.

**Role:** Structured monitoring phone calls with a sample of people who received support from our counsellors.

**Based:** Remote, from anywhere.

**Roster:** Unpaid standby pool from January 2027 to May 2029. Joining is not a job offer.

**Reports to:** M&E Lead.

**Contract:** Consultancy contract per campaign.

## **Why this roster**

New Pathways to Resilience (NPR) is a three-year project funded by the EU’s Asylum, Migration and Integration Fund (AMIF). It is built around Seefar’s Crisis Adaptation Mechanism (CAM), which lets the project respond when migration patterns shift. When a monitored indicator crosses its threshold, a campaign may be activated for a new audience or language, and Seefar then has two weeks to launch it. That is too short to recruit from scratch, so we keep an unpaid standby pool of vetted Counsellors, Social Media Officers and Monitoring Officers for 12 languages, ready to be contracted the moment a campaign is approved.

## **Who we are**

Seefar Foundation is a social enterprise with a simple mission: to transform the lives of vulnerable people. Through programmes rooted in technology, psychology and behaviour change, we help people build the skills and confidence they need to make a positive contribution to their communities. It’s how we support governments in finding solutions to challenges around irregular migration, poverty, human trafficking, violent extremism, access to justice, and more.

Our exceptional team of over 100 consultants are problem solvers and innovators, delivering programmes and high impact research. Together, we solve difficult, high impact problems for governments and NGOs across communications, digital, and research, monitoring and evaluation in Africa, Asia, and Europe.

## **Your Responsibilities**

1. Checkback calls (80%). Take part in a paid introductory training session and get to know the campaign, the checkback tools and the ethical guidelines for engaging with vulnerable people. Then conduct structured checkback calls by phone with a sample of people who received support from our counsellors at 3 weeks, 3 months or 12 months after their one-to-one support session with a Seefar counsellor. Administer the standardised checkback tools (Kobo forms) consistently on every call, capturing quantitative and qualitative data on wellbeing, migration decisions, referrals and satisfaction with the support received. Submit completed records within 24 hours of each call.
2. Data quality and learning (15%). Share observations on patterns in responses, data quality issues and anything that may affect the reliability of findings. Support translation or back-translation of M&E tools and templates between your language and English when needed. Manage your own call schedule and flag promptly when participants cannot be reached.
3. Independence and safeguarding (5%). Because checkbacks are a quality control process, stay independent of the counsellors and Social Media Officers delivering the campaign, so that outcome data remains neutral and credible. Treat all participant data with strict confidentiality in line with Seefar’s data protection standards, and escalate safeguarding concerns immediately.

## **Who you are**

**To succeed, you’ll need:**

- At least 3 years’ experience in monitoring and evaluation, data collection or a related field.
- Experience conducting structured telephone or remote surveys or interviews.
- Fluency in at least one roster language, and working proficiency in written and spoken English and/or Arabic and/or French.
- Computer literacy and a reliable internet connection.
- Strong interpersonal and communication skills, and the ability to engage sensitively with vulnerable people.
- The ability to work independently and remotely, and manage your own workload against deadlines.
- Strong attention to detail and organisational skills.
- A private, quiet space for confidential calls.
- The ability to work as an independent consultant and receive payments in EUR by international bank transfer.

You should meet all of the above. It’s a bonus if you have experience on humanitarian, development or migration-related programmes, familiarity with psychosocial support or returnee contexts, or experience using Kobo Toolbox or similar platforms.

## **How you work**

**Spoken/Written English and/or French and/or Arabic**

You write clear notes and observations in English and/or French and/or Arabic that others can act on.

**Roster language**

You interview fluently in one of these 12 languages: Pashto, Dari, Levantine Arabic, Sudanese Arabic, Bengali, Egyptian Arabic, Urdu, Moroccan Darija, Iraqi Arabic, Kurdish Sorani, Kurdish Badini, Somali.

**Structured interviewing**

You follow a questionnaire consistently, without sounding scripted.

**Sensitivity**

You put people at ease, recognise distress and respond with care.

**Data accuracy**

The data you collect is complete, consistent and entered within 24 hours.

**Independence**

You keep a clear boundary from the delivery team so data stays credible.

**Translation**

You translate and back-translate M&E tools accurately.

**Digital skills**

You are comfortable with Kobo or similar tools and Google Suite.

**Self regulation**

You respond constructively to professional and emotional challenges.

## **How the roster works**

- **It is not a job offer.** Joining the roster does not guarantee work, and you can work elsewhere in the meantime.
- **Everyone in the pool counts as equally qualified.** When a campaign is activated, we pick the best match on language, gender, location and availability. The reason for every choice is recorded.
- **When a campaign is approved,** we contact Monitoring Officers about six weeks before starting.
- **Quarterly check-ins.** Every three months we ask whether you want to stay, pause or leave, and whether you could start within your notice period. Missing one check-in makes your place dormant; missing two in a row means it expires and your data is deleted.
- **You remain on the roster** until you choose to leave, miss two check-ins in a row, or NPR ends in May 2029.

### **What we offer**

- Paid training once you are hired.
- Freedom to work elsewhere while on the roster, and to decline an offer without penalty.
- Work from anywhere, and return to the pool or apply for other Seefar roles after a campaign.
- Only months worked on an activated campaign are paid.

### **Who you’ll work with**

You will report to NPR’s M&E Lead. To keep outcome data neutral, you will work independently of the counsellors and Social Media Officers delivering the campaign, while sharing what you learn with the M&E team. You will join a team with a mix of perspectives, backgrounds, technical expertise and lived experience, working across Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia.

title: Counsellor - Roster
body:
**Counsellor - Roster**

**Summary**

**Languages:** One of 12 roster languages (Pashto, Dari, Levantine Arabic, Sudanese Arabic, Bengali, Egyptian Arabic, Urdu, Moroccan Darija, Iraqi Arabic, Kurdish Sorani, Kurdish Badini and Somali), plus English and/or Arabic and/or French.

**Role:** Remote one-to-one counselling, by phone, WhatsApp, Signal or Telegram for people considering irregular migration or already on the move.

**Based:** Remote, from anywhere.

**Roster:** Unpaid standby pool from January 2027 to May 2029. Joining is not a job offer.

**Reports to:** Project Coordinator, or a team leader on larger campaigns.

**Contract:** Consultancy contract per campaign.

## **Why this roster**

New Pathways to Resilience (NPR) is a three-year project funded by the EU’s Asylum, Migration and Integration Fund (AMIF). It is built around Seefar’s Crisis Adaptation Mechanism (CAM), which lets the project respond when migration patterns shift. When a monitored indicator crosses its threshold, a campaign may be activated for a new audience or language, and Seefar then has two weeks to launch it. That is too short to recruit from scratch, so we keep an unpaid standby pool of vetted Counsellors, Social Media Officers and Monitoring Officers for 12 languages, ready to be contracted the moment a campaign is approved.

## **Who we are**

Seefar Foundation is a social enterprise with a simple mission: to transform the lives of vulnerable people. Through programmes rooted in technology, psychology and behaviour change, we help people build the skills and confidence they need to make a positive contribution to their communities. It’s how we support governments in finding solutions to challenges around irregular migration, poverty, human trafficking, violent extremism, access to justice, and more.

Our exceptional team of over 100 consultants are problem solvers and innovators, delivering programmes and high impact research. Together, we solve difficult, high impact problems for governments and NGOs across communications, digital, and research, monitoring and evaluation in Africa, Asia, and Europe.

## **Your Responsibilities**

1. Remote counselling (50%). Provide confidential one-to-one consultations by phone, WhatsApp, Signal or Telegram, to people considering irregular migration and people already on the move. Give accurate, neutral information about the risks of irregular migration and safe, legal alternatives. Assess each person’s psychological distress and mental health needs, and respond appropriately, for example with empathetic listening, coping strategies, or grief and loss support.
2. Referrals and follow-up (40%). Follow up with individuals to match them with a suitable referral and accompany them through the process, including emotional, medical, livelihood and other support services where available. Maintain and update the campaign’s referral database so that it stays accurate and useful for the whole team.
3. Records, safeguarding and teamwork (10%). Keep timely, confidential records of every session. Flag safeguarding concerns immediately. Take part in paid training before consultations start, attend team meetings, recommend ways to improve the service, and stay reachable to your supervisor during working hours.

## **Who you are**

**To succeed, you’ll need:**

- At least 2 years’ professional experience as a counsellor or in a similar role.
- Experience delivering remote counselling and trauma-informed care.
- Fluency in English and/or Arabic and/or French and in at least one roster language.
- Demonstrated experience working with vulnerable people, and a thorough understanding of confidentiality.
- Experience working remotely across platforms such as Google Suite, and a reliable internet connection.
- A private, quiet space for confidential calls.
- The ability to work as an independent consultant and receive payments in EUR by international bank transfer.

You should meet all of the above. It’s a bonus if you have:

- A BA degree in Counselling, Social Work, Psychology or another mental health-related field.
- Knowledge of legal migration pathways relevant to your audience.
- Experience working with migrants from or in your audience’s countries.
- Experience counselling people experiencing crisis, loss, grief, suicidal ideation, depression or anxiety.

Women counsellors are especially needed for the Somali-speaking pool.

## **How you work**

**Spoken/Written English and/or French and/or Arabic**

You write clear notes and observations in English and/or French and/or Arabic that others can act on.

**Roster language**

You counsel fluently in one of these 12 languages: Pashto, Dari, Levantine Arabic, Sudanese Arabic, Bengali, Egyptian Arabic, Urdu, Moroccan Darija, Iraqi Arabic, Kurdish Sorani, Kurdish Badini, Somali.

**Empathy**

You stay calm, patient and present with people in distress.

**Assessment**

You recognise distress and mental health needs, and respond appropriately.

**Information**

You explain migration risks and safe, legal alternatives without judgement.

**Confidentiality**

You protect participants’ data and know when to raise safeguarding concerns.

**Record keeping**

You document every session on time, every time.

**Digital skills**

You are comfortable with using a laptop or phone and Google Suite.

**Self regulation**

You respond constructively to professional and emotional challenges.

## **How the roster works**

- **It is not a job offer.** Joining the roster does not guarantee work, and you can work elsewhere in the meantime.
- **Everyone in the pool counts as equally qualified.** When a campaign is activated, we pick the best match on language, gender, location and availability. The reason for every choice is recorded.
- **When a campaign is approved,** we contact counsellors about three weeks before starting.
- **Quarterly check-ins.** Every three months we ask whether you want to stay, pause or leave, and whether you could start within your notice period. Missing one check-in makes your place dormant; missing two in a row means it expires and your data is deleted.
- **You remain on the roster** until you choose to leave, miss two check-ins in a row, or NPR ends in May 2029.

### **What we offer**

- Paid training once you are hired.
- Freedom to work elsewhere while on the roster, and to decline an offer without penalty.
- Work from anywhere, and return to the pool or apply for other Seefar roles after a campaign.
- Only months worked on an activated campaign are paid.

### **Who you’ll work with**

You will report to the Project Coordinator, or to a team leader on larger campaigns, and work alongside other counsellors. The Social Media Officer’s campaign brings people to you, and Monitoring Officers later check back, independently, with a sample of the people you counselled. You will join a team with a mix of perspectives, backgrounds, technical expertise and lived experience, working across Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia.
