In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Chargé-e des Opérations - SENEGAL (JPO)
body:
**Entrée en fonction :** 1.12.26

**Durée :** 6 mois

**Lieu :** Dakar, Sénégal

**Statut :** non accompagné

Terre des hommes ne fixe pas de date de clôture pour ce poste ; le recrutement se poursuit jusqu'à ce que le poste soit pourvu.

**Tdh :**

La Fondation Terre des hommes (Tdh), dont le siège est à Lausanne et le bureau à Zurich, est la plus grande organisation suisse de défense des droits de l'enfant avec plus de 2000 collaborateurs et collaboratrices dans le monde. Nous nous engageons aux côtés des enfants pour garantir leurs droits, protéger leur vie et améliorer leur bien-être. Nous y parvenons grâce à nos programmes innovants dans les domaines de la santé, de la migration et de l'accès à la justice, conçus pour avoir un impact positif et durable.

**Contexte :**

Terre des hommes Lausanne (Tdh), fondée en 1960, est la plus grande organisation suisse de défense des droits de l'enfant. Tdh se consacre à apporter des changements significatifs et durables dans la vie des enfants et des jeunes, en particulier ceux et celles qui sont le plus en danger. Tdh est active dans une trentaine de pays, dans des contextes humanitaires et de développement.

En Afrique subsaharienne, Tdh intervient directement dans 8 pays (Burkina Faso, Burundi, Guinée-Conakry, Kenya Mali, Mauritanie, Nigeria et Sénégal,) et via des partenariats dans 6 autres pays (Benin, Cameroun, Madagascar, Niger, Togo et Ouganda).

Dans le cadre de la décentralisation de son modèle d'organisation, Tdh à ouvert un bureau régional à Dakar au Sénégal pour lequel un poste de Chargé.e des Opérations est ouvert.

**Responsabilités :**

Sous la supervision de la Conseillère Régionale en recherche de fonds, le.la Chargé.e des Opérations appuie le bureau régional et les équipes pays dans la mise en œuvre des activités liées aux subventions et à la collecte de fonds dans la région Afrique.

Ce poste contribue aux processus relatifs aux subventions et à la collecte de fonds — du suivi des opportunités à l'élaboration des propositions et au reporting auprès des bailleurs — tout en soutenant les efforts en matière d'engagement des bailleurs et de partenariats à l'échelle de la région.

Grant Acquisition Process

- Contribue à l'identification et au suivi des opportunités de financement pertinentes pour les programmes de Tdh dans la région Afrique.
- Appuie le développement et la soumission de propositions de projet régionales, multipays et pays : appui ou coordination du processus d’écriture, respect des procédures bailleurs, développement de plans d’action, écriture, traduction, enregistrement sur les plateformes de soumission.
- Contribue au contrôle qualité et à la finalisation des rapports pour des financements institutionnels tout en s’assurant de la soumission en temps voulu (suivi du calendrier et des échéances, relances lorsque nécessaire auprès des contributeurs, consolidation des données, etc.), conformément aux exigences contractuelles et aux normes de Tdh.
- Assure le suivi des besoins en cofinancement avec la CR Finance, appui l'élaboration de propositions et rapports de projets à destination de fondations en coordination avec le secteur philanthropie.
- Veille à ce que les informations relatives aux subventions et aux financements dans Engage360 et les GFU pays et région (système interne de Tdh) soient exactes et régulièrement mises à jour, et assure le suivi auprès des équipes concernées pour garantir l'exhaustivité des données. En cas d’absence de Chargé.e de Grant dans une délégation, assure directement la mise à jour des données pour le pays concerné.
- Appuie le développement des contrats de partenariats opérationnels (contenu, signature, archivage, etc.).
- Contribue à l’analyse des réponses aux demandes de financements institutionnels et philanthropiques.
- S’assure de la collecte et de l’archivage des documents institutionnels nécessaires à la signature des contrats en collaboration avec le siège, la région, les délégations et les partenaires.

Communication

- Appuie la relation avec les bailleurs de fonds et les partenaires, y compris la préparation de supports de recherche de fonds (ex. : témoignages, récits de réussite).
- Appuie le rapportage annuel à travers la vérification et la consolidation des données et informations projets, en coordination avec les équipes PREX, Q&A et Grants, ainsi qu’avec les autres parties prenantes concernées aux niveaux des délégations et de la région.
- Contribue à la communication interne liée aux projets (newsletter mensuelle, supports spécifiques, etc.) et consolide les éléments proposés par les délégations et la région, en veillant à la cohérence, à l’exactitude et à la qualité des informations rapportées.

*La description complète du poste sera communiquée aux candidats sélectionnés pour lancer le processus de recrutement.*

**Profil recherché**

**Formation :**

Etude supérieure (Master ou autre diplôme équivalant en relations internationales, développement ou autre domaine pertinent)

**Langues :**

Excellentes compétences linguistiques en Français et Anglais.

**Compétences :**

- Bonne compréhension de la gestion du cycle de projet dans les environnements de développement, d'urgence et de crises prolongées, notamment en Afrique
- Bonne compréhension du processus d’aquisition de financements.

**IT :** Maitrise des outils et applications usuels (Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, etc.)

**Conditions :**

Contrat suisse

Salaire mensuel brut CHF 2450- x13,36 mois

Assurances : maladie, accident, rapatriement

Congés annuels : 25 jours/an

Vols aller-retour vers le lieu d'affectation

**Code Global de Conduite et Politiques Ethiques de Tdh :**

S'engage à promouvoir et à respecter le Code de Conduite Global, à rapporter systématiquement toute violation du Code à travers les mécanismes formels de rapport de Tdh et à traiter toute violation des procédures et des processus de manière appropriée.

Sensibilise la Fondation aux risques de non-respect des politiques, de violence et d'abus, et aux droits qui en découlent, à l'égard des enfants, des membres de la communauté et de nos propres employé.e.s.

S'engage à respecter les principales politiques et directives éthiques, notamment la politique de sauvegarde, la politique de lutte contre la fraude et la corruption, la politique relative aux conflits d'intérêts et d'autres politiques liées à la prévention du financement du terrorisme et des activités criminelles, ainsi qu’au comportement sur le lieu de travail.

S'engage à mettre en pratique les valeurs et les principes en adoptant un comportement exemplaire, en parfaite adéquation avec le code de conduite, et en respectant toujours les procédures et les processus établis.

S'engage à développer une culture de management conforme et éclairée au sein de l'organisation et dans notre travail avec les enfants et les communautés dans lesquelles nous opérons.

title: Helios+ Center Assistant
body:
**BACKGROUND:** The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive and rebuild their lives. Founded in 1933, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. At work today in over 40 countries, the IRC aims to restore safety, dignity and hope to millions who are uprooted and struggling to endure. In response to the arrival of refugees in Greece in 2015, the IRC has been offering SMS, WASH and Protection services. Among others, through its child protection programs, the IRC has been offering individual support through case management to vulnerable children and their families, non-formal educational activities for children through Safe Healing and Learning Spaces and emergency accommodation and protection to unaccompanied children. Since 2019, IRC Hellas implements an alternative care project for unaccompanied children and will now pilot this project to Greek born children and adults.

**SCOPE OF WORK:** Helios+ - Comprehensive Actions for the integration of Third Country Nationals in the Labor Market - (MIS 6016874) is a portfolio of regional Integration Projects, dedicated to fostering the integration of third-country nationals into Greece's labor market and society. Designed by the International Organization for Migration (IOM) with the support of the Government of Greece (GoG), co-financed by the European Union under the Regional Programs (RP) for 2021–2027 and aligns fully with Greece's National Strategy for Integration. HELIOS+ is committed to empowering Beneficiaries of International and Temporary Protection residing in Greece by providing them with the tools and resources needed to achieve socio-economic independence and actively participate in the Greek community, while promoting self-reliance and inclusion through a comprehensive set of services tailored to the needs of the target group.

In the Attica Region, International Rescue Committee Hellas participates as a partner of IOM Greece, together with Solidarity Now, in the consortium led by Caritas Hellas.

The IRC supports access to job counseling and job matching, life skills, education and psychosocial support – directly and in collaboration with partners. The IRC is recruiting a HELIOS+ Center assistant for the reception and registration of beneficiaries, providing first-level information, and guiding beneficiaries to the specialized services of the center. The HELIOS+ Center assistant will also be responsible for preparing the necessary documents for their registration, monitoring the security of the center, and ensuring the smooth operation of the center’s overall spaces and equipment.

**RESPONSIBILITIES:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Welcome and receive beneficiaries and visitors to the Center warmly and friendly**;**
- Provide information about the Center and its services to the beneficiaries of the subproject, as required**;**
- Provide administrative support to ensure the smooth daily operation of the Center**;**
- Manage the Center’s calendar and scheduling of sessions, appointments, etc., in coordination with the Center’s Manager**;**
- Manage the Center’s correspondence and communications (phone/email/mail)**;**
- Update and maintain a contact list**;**
- Effectively maintain filing systems, both electronic and paper-based**;**
- Collect and organize the data required for each beneficiary;
- Monitor the Center’s spaces and their security, maintain cleanliness and order, aim to ensure smooth and efficient operation, in close cooperation with the Center’s Manager;
- Other related duties as assigned by the subproject Coordinator;
- Participate in regular team meetings and external meetings as requested;

**REQUIREMENTS:**

- BA/BS Degree in Pedagogical Studies, Administrative Studies, and/or other related fields;
- At least three (3) years of experience in a corresponding position of responsibility, preferably in the field of humanitarian organizations;
- Excellent knowledge of Greek and English, spoken and written (level C1/C2).
- Computer skills, in particular word processing, excel spreadsheets and internet services;
- Excellent interpersonal, team and communication skills;
- Ability to organize and prioritize workload using initiative;
- Ability to work under pressure;

**PREFERRED EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS:**

- Experience in customer service.
- Ability to manage multiple tasks.
- Intercultural awareness and flexibility.
- Ability to work on own initiative and at the same time as part of a multicultural and interdisciplinary team.
- Knowledge of French, or Arabic, or Farsi, or Pashto, or Urdu is an advantage.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT:**

Working hours: 9:00-17:00

Travel and other requirements: Occasionally to other areas of IRC programs within Athens

**This position is expected to end on May 30, 2027.**

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: £1,300 - £1,590/month). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

title: Project Development Consultant (Fiji Nationals Only)
body:
Job Identification (Reference Number): **23660**  
Position Title: **Project Development Consultant (Fiji Nationals Only)**  
Duty Station City: **Suva**  
Duty Station Country: **Fiji**  
Contract Type: **Consultant A**  
*Recruiting Type:* **Consultancy**  
*Vacancy Type:* **Call for Applications**  
Initial duration: **6 months**  
Closing date: **02 November 2026**

**Context:**

The IOM Coordination Office for the South Pacific in Suva, Fiji supports programme development, resource mobilization, donor relations, and programme oversight across multiple Pacific Island Countries. As the Pacific portfolio continues to expand in areas including climate mobility, disaster risk reduction, labour mobility, border governance, protection, and humanitarian preparedness and response, additional surge support is required to strengthen project development and donor engagement efforts.

Under the overall supervision of the Head of Programme Support Unit and direct supervision of the Programme Development Officer, the consultant will support the Programme Support Unit in the development of concept notes, project proposals, resource mobilization, partnership engagement activities and programme information products. The consultant will work closely with programme teams and relevant IOM offices to ensure timely and high-quality project development processes. This consultancy will contribute to strengthening the Mission's project pipeline, resource mobilization, and programme quality assurance mechanisms across the South Pacific region.

**Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing:**

Programme Support Unit (PSU)

IOM Coordination Office for the South Pacific, Suva, Fiji.

**Description for Internal Candidates**

**Responsibilities for Internal Candidates**

- Assist in the development of results-based concept notes, project proposals, budgets and supporting documentation in accordance with IOM, donor and UN requirements.
- Compile, summaries, analyze, and present information/data on specific project topics, highlighting noteworthy issues on donor priorities, funding opportunities, regional trends and emerging programme needs to support resource mobilization efforts.
- Support coordination with programme managers, technical specialists, regional offices and external partners during project development and donor reporting processes.
- Maintain project development tracking systems and programme support unit information share points.
- Assist in organizing donor meetings, consultations, workshops, missions, and partnership engagement activities, including preparation of background materials and meeting summaries, when required.
- Contribute to the preparation of visibility materials, success stories, factsheets, programme summaries and external communication products.
- Provide support to programme reviews and information requests from donors, governments, regional organizations, headquarters and regional offices.
- Perform such other related duties as may be assigned.

**Performance indicators for the evaluation of results**

- Timely completion of assigned project development and coordination tasks.
- Quality and accuracy of concept notes, proposals and briefing materials produced.
- Compliance with IOM project development and donor standards.
- Number of contributions to proposal development and resource mobilization processes.
- Timely response to information requests and programme support requirements.
- Maintenance of accurate project development and resource mobilization records.
- Demonstrated professionalism, accountability and adherence to IOM policies and procedures.

**Qualifications for Internal Candidates**

- Bachelor’s degree in Political Science, Social Science, International Relations, Development Studies, Migration Studies, Human Rights, Law or a related field from an accredited academic institution with four years of relevant professional experience; or,
- High School diploma with six years of relevant professional experience.

**Experience**

- Experience in project development and proposal writing for bilateral and multilateral donors.
- Experience working with international organizations, development agencies, government institutions or non-governmental organizations.
- Experience coordinating with multiple stakeholders and working in multicultural environments.
- Experience in the other Pacific countries is an advantage.

**Skills**

- Knowledge of drafting, proposal writing, editing and analytical skills.
- Knowledge of UN and bilateral donor programming.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications.
- Knowledge of Results-Based Management and monitoring frameworks.
- Excellent written and spoken English.

**Languages**

- Language: Excellent command of English
- For this consultancy, Fluency in English language is required.
- Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

**Travel required**

- NO

**Required Competencies**

IOM’s competency framework can be found at [this link](https://www.iom.int/sites/g/files/tmzbdl486/files/about-iom/Competency_Framework-EN.pdf). Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these three values:

- Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
- Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
- Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.

title: Logistics coordinator (F/M) - Syria
body:
Do you want to join a committed, activist-driven organization and take meaningful action for social justice?  
For over 40 years, Médecins du Monde has been delivering healthcare to the most vulnerable, challenging barriers to access, and driving long-term change in health policies.

In France and across nearly 30 countries, our work is built around six core missions:

- Sexual and reproductive health and rights (including access to safe abortion)
- Migration, exile, human rights and health
- Harm reduction
- Health and the environment
- Healthcare systems
- Humanitarian spaces

**MdM in Syria**

Since December 2024, about 1.8 million refugees and 2 million internally displaced people have returned to their areas of origin (UNHCR, 1 October 2026, indicative), and many others remain displaced. Many return to areas where roads, public services, and health facilities are damaged or only partially functional. Humanitarian needs remain high, while access, administrative procedures and security conditions can change quickly from one area to another.

Médecins du Monde (MdM) works in Syria to protect vulnerable people's access to essential health care, including returnees and displaced communities. Our programs are run from the coordination office in Damascus, with teams and partners in several governorates.

MdM is currently operating in Aleppo and Idlib governorates, supporting three health facilities. Since 2026, program activities have been extended to Rural Damascus and Daraa governorates, where MdM will support two health centers.

**About the role**

You will provide strategic and technical leadership to the logistics team, support program planning and proposal development, manage logistics risks and ensures compliance with MdM France procedures, donor requirements, and applicable Syrian regulations.

**What you’ll do**

Under the supervision of the general coordinator, you define, plan and implement all supply and logistics activities, while ensuring budget compliance and respect of MdM’s protocols and procedures. You lead and manage the logistics team.

More specifically, your main responsibilities are:

- Define, plan and budget logistical needs for the mission and monitor logistical activities
- Define, implement and adapt procurement plan and procedures
- Manage contracts related to logistics and supply activities
- Recruit and manage the logistics team, set objectives, define training needs, ensure skills management
- Ensure monitoring and reporting on logistical activities, adapt indicators when needed
- Supervise and manage the transportation of goods and people
- Supervise the installation and maintenance of office and accommodation areas
- Define and monitor IT and communication resources
- Ensure that the archiving system for logistics documents is respected
- Participate in the definition, implementation and monitoring of the safety and security standards
- Provide logistics guidance, training, advising and technical support to all field teams

**Who you’ll work with**

You will work closely with the logistics advisor at HQ, the program coordinators and the health managers, the support coordinators, the MEAL team and the security focal point, among others.

**You are the right match if you:**

- Hold a Master’s degree in the following : logistics, supply chain management, procurement, business administration or a related field.
- Have at least 5 years of relevant professional experience, including experience in a coordination or management role in a humanitarian or international NGO setting.
- Have experience managing local and international supply chains, preferably including medicines and health commodities.
- Have a previous experience with Médecins du Monde (strong asset)
- Speak English fluently, Arabic is highly appreciated

**This role may not suit you if you:**

- Don't have experience in premises management, infrastructure, energy systems and rehabilitation or renovation works.
- Don't have the ability to work under pressure, in complex, restrictive and volatile operational environments.
- You are not aligned with MdM’s values and activist approach

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow during the month of October.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)  
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

**Ready to apply?**

We only need your CV and a cover letter.  
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

**Employment conditions**

title: Training Officer, Cultural Orientation
body:
**Job Overview:** The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is one of the leading providers of high-quality programming for refugees resettling to the United States. The IRC is committed to developing innovative programs that respond to the refugees’ unique strengths and needs, using our learning and experience to shape policy and practice, and highlighting and promoting best practices in refugee services provision.

The IRC is seeking a Training Officer, Cultural Orientation for Switchboard, an Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR)-funded program. Switchboard is a one-stop resource hub for refugee service providers in the United States. Switchboard provides training and capacity-building services to service providers in the United States, including resettlement agencies and affiliates, state agencies, ethnic community-based organizations, and others. More information about Switchboard can be found at [www.SwitchboardTA.org](https://reliefweb.int/file:///C:UsersTigestCoAppDataLocalMicrosoftOlkAttachmentsooa-fefcb179-4b91-4707-b044-59e9496f57fe69780562696ebcadf2340c5c93711aeb96e9493d8b84ea912d714b7dd9c61fdbwww.SwitchboardTA.org).

Settle In is Switchboard's digital information service for newcomers taking the knowledge and resources Switchboard offers to service providers and adapting and delivering it directly to newcomers**,** in multiple languages, through its website (SettleInUS.org), mobile app, and social media platforms. More information on Settle In can be found on https://www.settleinus.org/.

Cultural orientation is a core service in refugee resettlement in the United States, helping newcomers build the knowledge and skills to navigate life in their new communities. The Training Officer, Cultural Orientation, leads the development and delivery of capacity-building initiatives for these programs. This includes training and technical assistance (TTA) to service providers, helping them build strong cultural orientation programs and apply best practices when working with newcomers. This staff member is responsible for producing and maintaining high-quality performance by collaborating with experts, designing effective cultural orientation resources such as curricula, training materials, and learning tools, and facilitating learning experiences that improve outcomes for newcomer children, adults, and families. This role requires hands-on experience working directly with clients, subject matter experts, and partners, along with prior experience delivering cultural orientation to newcomers.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Training and Technical Assistance**

- Design and deliver versatile cultural orientation training to service providers and cultural orientation delivery staff.
- Provide responsive and cross-disciplinary technical assistance to refugee service providers in response to cultural orientation TTAs, adapting content to meet varied organizational needs and learning styles.
- In collaboration with colleagues across teams, develop written and multimedia learning resources (e.g., toolkits, videos, podcasts) that reflect trauma-informed, client-centered, and strength-based approaches.
- Adapt materials for different literacy levels, languages, and cultural contexts
- Integrate feedback from internal and external reviewers to continuously improve training and resource contents and delivery methods.
- Facilitate communities of practice and peer learning groups to promote knowledge exchange and cross-training across service areas.

**Project Management**

- Contribute to the creation of Switchboard’s annual training and technical assistance (TTA) workplan.
- Ensure related trainings and learning resources are developed and delivered on time and on budget.
- Use effective communication and collaborative skills with a wide range of stakeholders
- Manage internal and external subject matter expert/consultant relationships and project plans as they contribute to the development of related TTA.

**Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E)**

- Oversee tracking of related TTA outputs and outcomes against targets (materials developed, trainings delivered, individuals participating, etc.)
- Together with Training Officers and Switchboard’s M&E team, review and analyze feedback data from related TTA participants
- Oversee provision of inputs into Switchboard reports, including monthly activity updates and semi-annual Performance Progress Reports.

- Other duties as assigned

**Job Requirements:**

**Required:**

- Bachelor's degree required, preferably in a related field such as Education, International Development, Social Work, Public Administration, Cross-Cultural Studies, Migration/Refugee Studies, or a related social science (or equivalent experience).
- Minimum 6 years of direct service experience with refugees and/or other ORR-eligible populations
- Experience delivering cultural orientation to newcomers
- Experience providing training and/or technical assistance to build the capacity of refugee service providers
- Experience providing client-centered, trauma-informed, and strength-based services for refugees
- Experience in supporting newcomers' access and gaining self-sufficiency for services and resources i.e. financial, medical, social, vocational etc.

**Preferred:**

- Lived experience with forced displacement or shared background with newcomer populations
- Experience managing external subject matter experts and/or consultants
- Experience contributing to project M&E (data collection, management, and reporting)
- Experience with evidence-based programming

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:**

- Working knowledge of programs and services related to client-centered services for refugees and newcomer families
- Strong understanding of cultural orientation frameworks, refugee/newcomer integration principles, and adult learning principles
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with fluency in English; including engaging public speaking abilities
- Self-starter with ability to work both independently and collaboratively as a part of a team
- Capacity to give and receive constructive feedback
- Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple competing deadlines and efficient time management
- Adequate technology literacy including intermediate knowledge of MS Office Suite (Teams, Word, PowerPoint, Excel), and Zoom, with adaptability to learning new and innovative technology.
- Strong attention to detail

***Language Skills:*** Fluent in written and spoken English***.***

**Working Environment:** This position is a remote working environment. Required domestic travel up to 20%.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $80,000 - $85,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Medical Coordinator (F/M) - Afghanistan
body:
Do you want to join a committed, activist-driven organization and take meaningful action for social justice?

For over 40 years, Médecins du Monde has been delivering healthcare to the most vulnerable, challenging barriers to access, and driving long-term change in health policies.

In France and across nearly 30 countries, our work is built around six core missions:

- Sexual and reproductive health and rights (including access to safe abortion)
- Migration, exile, human rights and health
- Harm reduction
- Health and the environment
- Healthcare systems
- Humanitarian spaces

## MdM in Afghanistan

Médecins du Monde re-opened its mission in Afghanistan in 2021 and currently implements programmes in primary healthcare, sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR), mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), nutrition and harm reduction through a combination of direct implementation and partnerships with local organizations. The mission operates in a complex environment marked by restrictions imposed by de facto authorities, constraints affecting women’s participation and access to services, evolving humanitarian needs and significant challenges for the health system. Current programmes are implemented in Wardak, Farah and Nimroz provinces and place a strong emphasis on community engagement, quality of care and access to essential health services.

## About the role

You will join the mission at a pivotal moment. Beyond ensuring the quality and relevance of medical activities, you will play a key role in strengthening the mission’s medical leadership, supporting teams, reinforcing SRHR priorities and helping to structure programmes, partnerships and ways of working in line with Médecins du Monde’s values and standards. Working closely with the General Coordinator, HQ Health Advisor and programme teams, you will contribute directly to improving access to quality healthcare for vulnerable populations across Afghanistan.

## What you'll do

? Define, drive and monitor the mission's medical strategy and ensure its alignment with MdM's global priorities, with a particular focus on SRHR.

? Ensure the quality, relevance and effectiveness of health, nutrition, MHPSS and SRHR activities across all programmes.

? Lead, support and develop medical teams through coaching, capacity-building and performance management.

? Analyse programme performance and medical data to guide decision-making and continuous improvement.

? Design new projects, contribute to donor proposals and support the mission's strategic development.

? Represent MdM with health authorities, humanitarian actors, partners and community stakeholders.

? Adapt programmes and priorities in response to contextual changes, population needs and humanitarian emergencies.

## Who you'll work with

You will report directly to the General Coordinator and maintain a strong functional relationship with the Health Advisor based at headquarters. You will supervise a technical medical team of two to three people and work closely with programme managers, medical supervisors, support departments and local partners across the mission. The position also requires regular interaction with health authorities, UN agencies, humanitarian coordination mechanisms and community representatives.

## What you'll gain

- Develop advanced leadership skills in one of the world's most complex humanitarian contexts.
- Strengthen your expertise in SRHR programming, community-based health approaches and health system strengthening.Gain significant experience in humanitarian negotiation, representation and stakeholder engagement
- Contribute to meaningful, high-impact programmes supporting vulnerable communities while helping shape the future strategic direction of the mission.
- Propose and develop projects relating to women’s rights and health, in collaboration with local organisations.

### REQUIREMENTS

## You are the right match if you:

- Demonstrate a strong commitment to human rights, non-discrimination and respectful engagement, even in sensitive contexts where values, beliefs or lifestyles differ significantly from your own.
- Can provide strategic medical leadership and bring structure, clarity and direction to complex health programmes.
- Lead teams through trust, listening, accountability and collaboration while fostering a healthy and inclusive work environment.
- Have successfully strengthened the quality, relevance and impact of SRHR or public health programmes.
- Build productive relationships and negotiate effectively with authorities, partners and diverse stakeholders in challenging environments.
- Remain calm, analytical and decisive when responding to emergencies, operational constraints or rapidly changing contexts.

## This role may not suit you if:

- You favour directive or individualistic approaches over collaboration, dialogue and collective problem-solving.
- You struggle to provide constructive management, clear communication and respectful feedback.
- You are uncomfortable representing humanitarian principles and advocating for vulnerable populations in sensitive environments.
- You prefer highly structured and predictable settings over complex and evolving humanitarian contexts.
- You are not aligned with Médecins du Monde's values, principles and activist approach.

## Recruitment process

Apply soon! If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)  
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

## Ready to apply?

We only need your CV and a cover letter.

If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we'd love to hear from you!

### **EMPLOYMENT CONDITIONS**

**Contract & status:**

- Gross monthly salary: € 3,664
- Fixed-term contract (6 months), starting as soon as possible
- Single posting

**Work environment:**

- Position based in Kabul, Afghanistan

**Benefits:**

- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Accommodation: in a guesthouse with other expatriates initially, with the possibility of individual housing later on
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility

**Essentials:**

title: Coordinateur logistique voltigeur - Worldwide (F/H)
body:
Vous souhaitez intégrer une association militante et agir concrètement pour plus de justice sociale ?

Médecins du Monde agit depuis plus de 40 ans pour soigner les populations les plus vulnérables, dénoncer les entraves à l’accès aux soins et faire évoluer durablement les politiques de santé.

En France et dans près de 30 pays, nos actions s’articulent autour de six combats politiques :

- droits et santé sexuels et reproductifs (dont le droit à l’avortement)
- migration, exil, droits et santé
- réduction des risques
- santé environnement
- droits et système de santé
- espaces humanitaires

## **Pourquoi nous avons besoin de vous**

Les interventions d’urgence face aux crises, conflits, catastrophes naturelles, sont l’un des axes prioritaires d’intervention pour Médecins du Monde. Notre indépendance financière, la force de nos partenariats, l'implication et la flexibilité de nos équipes sont autant d’éléments clés pour apporter une réponse efficace à ces catastrophes.

Le mandat de la Cellule Urgence est d’intervenir en priorité sur les urgences et crises qui surviennent dans les pays où MdM est déjà opérationnel (30 pays). La réponse d’urgence dans les pays où MdM n’est pas présent est systématiquement considéré si l’accès au continuum de soins est interrompu et si les capacités du pays et des acteurs sur place sont dépassées.

MdM fournit également un appui et une expertise opérationnelle et technique aux missions des pôles géographiques sur leurs réponses d’urgences.

Vous faites partie de l’équipe voltigeur.euse.s de la Cellule Urgence qui est donc déployée dans les contextes d’urgence pour lancer de nouvelles interventions et/ou renforcer les équipes existantes. Vous pouvez également être déployé.e pour participer à des missions exploratoires, participer à l’ouverture de nouvelles missions et/ou de nouvelles bases, appuyer les opérations/missions existantes MdM à travers du « gap-filling » ou appuyer la mise en œuvre d’activités spécifiques liées aux activités logistiques (ex : formation, préparation, etc.).

## **Vos missions**

Vos principales responsabilités sont :

- Piloter la stratégie logistique de la mission et en assurer la mise en œuvre
- Coordonner et superviser l’ensemble des activités logistiques : chaîne d’approvisionnement, parc de véhicules, gestion des stocks, équipements, bâtiments, infrastructures informatiques, moyens de communication et énergie
- Animer et renforcer les capacités de l’équipe
- Appuyer également le/la coordinateur·rice général·e dans le suivi des procédures de sécurité
- Veiller au respect et à la bonne application des procédures MdM et bailleurs, et contribuer à garantir la qualité, l’efficacité et la conformité des services logistiques au sein de la mission, tout en œuvrant à la prévention et à la lutte contre la fraude et la corruption

Le partage du temps de travail entre le terrain et le siège est évaluée à 80%-20%.

La durée d’un déploiement sur le terrain est de trois 3 mois maximum, et est suivie par un temps de récupération.

## **Vos collègues**

Vous travaillez sous la responsabilité du responsable de la Cellule urgences basé au siège. Lorsque vous êtes déployé.e sur le terrain, vous reportez directement au/à la coordinateur.rice général.e de la mission. Vous avez un lien fonctionnel avec le/la référent.e logistique basé.e au siège. Vous collaborez avec les coordinateur.rice.s support ainsi qu'avec le/la chargé.e d'accès humanitaire & risques et les équipes programme.

## PROFIL

**Vous êtes la bonne personne si :**

- Vous avez une formation supérieure bac+2 type achat ou logistique
- Vous justifiez d'une expérience professionnelle de 5 ans (dont minimum 1 an sur un poste en coordination logistique dans le milieu humanitaire ou de minimum 2 ans d'expérience en tant que logisticien)
- Vous avez une solide résistance au stress et une capacité à vous adapter dans des contextes sécuritaires complexes
- Vous maitrisez le Pack Office
- Vous maitrisez l’anglais et le français couramment à l’écrit comme à l’oral

**Ce poste n'est pas pour vous si :**

- La flexibilité et l’adaptabilité ne comptent pas parmi vos principales qualités ; les déplacements fréquents ainsi que les changements réguliers d’équipe vous posent des difficultés
- Vous craignez de ne pas vous retrouver dans les valeurs et le positionnement militant de Médecins du Monde.

## Les prochaines étapes

Si votre candidature est sélectionnée, nous vous contacterons pour vous proposer un entretien RH avec notre chargée de recrutement. Puis viendront l'entretien technique et managérial (auquel des cas pratiques pourront éventuellement être intégrés).

Dans le cadre de la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme, des vérifications d’antécédents sur listes internationales pourront être effectuées. Les données sont traitées de façon confidentielle et sécurisée. Plus d’infos : [http://bit.ly/3CSThBs](http://bit.ly/3CSThBs)

Un extrait de casier judiciaire (B3) sera demandé à toute personne recrutée.

## Nous attendons votre candidature

Nous n’avons besoin que de votre CV et de votre lettre de motivation.

Si vous pensez correspondre à ce poste, n’attendez plus, postulez !

## VOS CONDITIONS D'EMPLOI

**Contrat & statut :**

- CDD à pourvoir dès que possible et jusqu'au 31/12/2026
- Salaire brut mensuel de 3 392 €
- Statut : agent de maitrise
- Poste à temps plein

**Les avantages :**

- Télétravail ponctuel
- 13e mois (pour les salarié.e.s ayant plus de 6 mois d’ancienneté)
- Prime de déplacement terrain de 198,18€ brut/mois au prorata du temps de présence sur le terrain
- Au siège, tickets restaurants d’une valeur unitaire de 10€ (participation à hauteur de 60% de MdM, 40% salarié.e) et sur le terrain via une allocation forfaitaire de restauration fixée en fonction du pays
- Au siège, remboursement du titre de transport en commun à 50% (abonnement mensuel) et prise en charge à 100% des allers-retours siège-terrain
- Logement pris en charge sur le terrain à 100%
- Mutuelle prise en charge à 100%
- MdM favorise la formation et la mobilité interne

**Les indispensables :**

- 5 semaines de congés + 22,5 RTT par an
- Engagement fort en faveur de l’inclusion et de la lutte contre toutes les discriminations
- Plus d’infos : [https://bit.ly/3x5MezL](https://bit.ly/3x5MezL)

**Cadre de travail :**

- Poste basé au siège à Saint-Denis (20% du temps) et sur les terrains internationaux (80% du temps)
- Déploiement sur le terrain pas avant 1 mois d’intégration
- Travail sur écran, en open space
- Communication orale et téléphonique
- Posture assise prolongée

**Diversité et inclusion**

MdM s’engage pour l’insertion des personnes en situation de handicap et lutte contre toutes les discriminations.

Si vous bénéficiez d’une reconnaissance de la qualité de travailleur.se handicapé.e et/ou si vous avez besoin d’un aménagement de poste, n’hésitez pas à nous en faire part.

title: Caseworker (Dari speaking)
body:
**IRC Background:** The mission of the International Rescue Committee (IRC) is to help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover and gain control of their future. Founded in 1933, the IRC has a presence in over 40 countries and 27 offices in the United States; the IRC leads the way from harm to home. Domestically, our offices across the U.S. ensure new arrivals have food, shelter, and clothing, and work with refugees to help them gain self-sufficiency.

**Job Overview:** The UHP Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other qualified immigrants to support a positive resettlement experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency. The UHP Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Coordinate timely pre- and post-arrival services to ensure each client has living essentials such as housing, food, medical care, and access to transportation, and is oriented to their new environment.
- Provide comprehensive, client-centered case management services including but not limited to accessing public benefits, housing, mental health services, medical care, school and ESL enrollment, referrals to community service providers, and assistance with booking appointments and scheduling transportation and interpretation.
- Conduct intake services with clients to assess needs. Develop self-sufficiency plans and timelines in partnership with each client. Provide individualized support through direct services, referrals, and advocacy.
- Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals, address challenges, and to ensure that available resources are utilized.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information in database(s) and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations. Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- May train and lead the activities of volunteers and interns.
- Work cross different programs as needed
- Other duties as assigned.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position reports to:** OIRS Casework Supervisor

**Position directly supervises:** N/A

**Indirect Reporting: Other Internal and/or external contacts:**

***Internal:***IRC Employees and program departments across Sacramento

***External:***IRC partners and other community agencies

**Job Requirements:**

- Associate or BA degree with an emphasis in Social Work, Migration Studies, Public Health, Refugee Studies, Development, Immigration Law, or an equivalent field of study; or 1+ years of related professional experience; preferably with asylum-seeking families, refugees, internally displaced persons, or individuals without status.
- Relevant professional experience in human services field required; minimum of 2 years’ experience strongly preferred.
- Experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations strongly preferred.
- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build internal and external relationships.
- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to multi-task, prioritize duties, and manage time effectively.
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
- Fluent in English, both spoken and written; proficiency Dari/Farsi and Pashto spoken by IRC’s clients.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research and problem-solving purposes.
- Commitment to teamwork and collaboration across all of IRC’s programs.
- Understanding of the U.S. immigration system and the rights of immigrants.
- Comfortability collaborating with governmental agencies and community providers.
- Ability to maintain accurate and up-to-date physical and electronic files and detailed case notes, enter required data in a timely manner, meet all case reporting requirements within established timelines and standards.
- Excellent writing and organizational skills with the ability to effectively summarize large amounts of information and maintain records of case progress achieved
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.
- This position will work from the IRC office in Sacramento.
- Offices hours are scheduled as Monday-Friday, 9:00am-5pm.

***This position is expected to end on September 30, 2027.***

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $29.10 - $30/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

title: Communications and Advocacy Officer
WARN Mental Health Advocate
body:
This position is represented by the OPEIU union and subject to the terms and conditions of a collective bargaining agreement.

**IRC Background:** The mission of the International Rescue Committee (IRC) is to help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover and gain control of their future. Founded in 1933, the IRC has a presence in over 40 countries and 27 offices in the United States; the IRC leads the way from harm to home. IRC opened an office in Seattle in 1976 and provides a continuum of services including intensive case management, employment and economic empowerment services, immigration assistance, health and wellness programming, and education support to refugee and immigrant families in Washington State. IRC Seattle is committed to providing trauma-informed, equitable, and accessible services and maintaining and evolving a diverse, inclusive, and supportive workplace.

**Job Overview:**

The Mental Health Advocate supports the mental health and resilience of survivors of trafficking through the WARN program, providing one-on-one peer support, referrals, and group-based services. This client-facing role includes one on one support, offering psychoeducation and skill-building workshops, and facilitating MHPSS groups. The Mental Health Advocate also coordinates program logistics, recruit participants, documents services, and supports evaluation through data collection. Additionally, they connect clients to appropriate mental health resources, assist with care coordination, and collaborate with supervisors to provide crisis support as needed.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Client Engagement & Support**

- Provide Psychosocial support including manualized interventions to clients. (Training in interventions will be provided.)
- Develop individualized action plans with clearly defined goals and activities based on assessment findings.
- With support from supervisor, provide health navigation services through referrals for clients requiring higher levels of mental health care to culturally and linguistically appropriate providers.
- Support crisis assessment and intervention for program participants in collaboration with supervisor.
- Represent the WARN Mental Health program at external and internal outreach events.

**Program Facilitation**

- Facilitate psychosocial group programs, ensuring alignment with contract guidelines.
- Facilitate psychoeducation and skill-building group sessions using evidence-based approaches under supervision.
- Recruit and enroll participants for WARN programs.
- Plan and organize logistics for WARN programs, including scheduling, transportation, materials, and space coordination.

**Monitoring & Evaluation**

- Prepare and administer Participant Service Reports with guidance from supervisor.
- Document client interactions and program activities through detailed case notes and data entry.
- Assist in evaluating current services and identifying opportunities for new program offerings.
- Use IRC software to document client information and other program materials.

**Administrative & Team Support**

- Attend and actively participate in team meetings, staff meetings, and relevant IRC trainings and conference calls.
- Collaborate with supervisor and team members to ensure program quality and compliance.
- Perform other duties as assigned to support the success of WARN programming.

title: Community Kitchen Supervisor at Habibi.Works
body:
## **About Habibi.Works**

Habibi.Works is a solidarity-based makerspace and community hub located next to the refugee camp of Katsikas in Northern Greece. It provides access to tools, knowledge, and shared spaces for people on the move, local residents, and international volunteers.

Rooted in values of solidarity, mutual respect, and justice, the project fosters community, agency, and resilience in a context shaped by European migration policies.

## **Role Description**

The kitchen supervisor is responsible for managing the kitchen, daily cooking, and food distribution at Habibi.Works. Works with community participants.

**Primary responsibilities:**

- Oversee ingredients and materials; coordinate with Procurement/Logistics Officer for weekly food shopping.
- Facilitate daily food preparation; ensure safe use of kitchen equipment; guide participants.
- Ensure appropriate quantities are prepared and distributed fairly.
- Maintain hygiene and cleanliness; encourage good practices.

**Secondary responsibilities:**

- Monitor kitchen equipment; sort broken or unneeded items; communicate material needs.
- Document kitchen activities.
- Collaborate with team members; ensure groceries are handled by Procurement/Logistics Officer.

**Skills and Experience**

- Basic cooking skills.
- Time management and adaptability.
- Ability to work in changing teams and under potential stress.

## **Requirements:**

- Commitment: minimum 6 weeks, up to 3 months
- Minimum age: 22
- Ability to live in the EU for duration of stay (we cannot support with visa processes)

## **What we offer:**

- Shared accommodation
- Meals on working days
- Two weekend days (Sunday & Monday)
- A meaningful role in a grassroots, solidarity-based project

title: Sewing Atelier Supervisor at Habibi.Works
body:
## **About Habibi.Works**

Habibi.Works is a solidarity-based makerspace and community hub located next to the refugee camp of Katsikas in Northern Greece. It provides access to tools, knowledge, and shared spaces for people on the move, local residents, and international volunteers.

Rooted in values of solidarity, mutual respect, and justice, the project fosters community, agency, and resilience in a context shaped by European migration policies.

## **Role Description**

Our Sewing Atelier Supervisor is responsible for managing the sewing atelier so that people have the opportunity to use the workshop and sewing machines independently, but also to gain and enhance their skills with sewing machines, textiles and tailoring. The Sewing Workshop is a heavily used working area in Habibi.Works with both very skilled tailors coming to use the space, as well as people who have no experience with sewing machines yet.

### **Primary responsibilities:**

- Make sure people use the machines correctly. If you see someone misusing a machine, offer your help; it is about education and empowerment. Show someone how to use the tools correctly and then encourage them to use the machine correctly
- Manage the material stock. Sort out material that is not needed and document if any material is missing. Communicate needs to the relevant team member and support in sourcing new materials
- Manage the even distribution of materials and adhere to our guidelines on material use per individual project (2 metres per 3 weeks)
- Support people in realizing their projects; guide people through the design and building process if needed
- Ensure the space is clean and tidy / materials are put back after use. Engage participants in this!
- Keep an eye on the machines and tools. If anything breaks, communicate this to the relevant team member to find a solution
- Ensure participants adhere to Habibi.Works’ “making, not taking” policy i.e. only completed projects can be taken home, not raw/unworked material

### **Secondary responsibilities:**

- Manage the distribution of weekly appointments for the sewing atelier; there is a dedicated appointment distribution given the demand for new fabric
- Documentation of the activities and creation of guides for various projects

### **Skills and Experience**

- Basic sewing skills, particularly pattern-making, clothing design and creation
- Knowledge of maintenance and set up of sewing machines
- (Desirable) Knowledge of embroidery, quilting and designing

## **Requirements:**

- Commitment: minimum 6 weeks
- Minimum age: 22
- Ability to live in the EU for duration of stay (we cannot support with visa processes)

## **What we offer:**

- Shared accommodation
- Meals on working days
- Two weekend days (Sunday & Monday)
- A meaningful role in a grassroots, solidarity-based project
- Possibility to extend to a long term contract after 3 months

title: Internship at USCRI El Salvador
body:
**About United States Committee for Refugees and Immigrants**

The U.S. Committee for Refugees and Immigrants (USCRI), established in 1911, is a nongovernmental, not-for-profit international organization dedicated to addressing the needs and rights of refugees and immigrants.

**About the REDII Bridges of Life Program**

The REDII Bridges of Life Project is an initiative of USCRI El Salvador, implemented in collaboration with Ministry of Foreign Affairs of El Salvador, aimed at supporting the sustainable reintegration of returned migrants through technical-vocational training, psychosocial support, and employment or entrepreneurship opportunities.

Through a comprehensive approach, the program identifies each participant’s immediate needs and connects them with essential services, including access to legal documentation, temporary financial assistance, and personalized case support.

Over its 10 years of implementation, the program has supported more than 1,200 Salvadorans in their return process, strengthening their skills, promoting economic self-sufficiency, and reducing risk factors associated with repeated migration.

**About the Internship**

The internship program at USCRI El Salvador seeks individuals with a strong social commitment and interest in contributing to the reintegration process of returned migrants.

Interns will work directly with the technical team of the REDII Bridges of Life Project in different areas, depending on their interests, academic background, and professional skills.

**Areas of Support and Responsibilities**

Responsibilities will vary depending on the assigned area and may include:

**1. General Support**

- Assisting in the implementation and follow-up of project activities.
- Supporting data collection and information systematization related to participants.
- Assisting with training sessions and technical vocational workshops.

**2. Communications**

- Preparing informational materials, success stories, and progress reports.
- Supporting coordination of events, training, and community meetings.
- Providing photographic documentation and assisting with institutional social media content.

**Profile**

- Completed bachelor's degree in international relations, Social Work, Psychology, Migration, or related studies.
- Fluency in Spanish.
- Experience in work, volunteer, or internship roles within organizations or areas related to migration, human rights, or vulnerable populations is desirable.
- Effective communication and active listening.
- Flexibility and adaptability.

**Internship Specifications**

- Full-time, in the city of San Salvador, El Salvador. (Six months).
- Start on July 01
- Unpaid internship
- Housing is provided.
- Medical coverage or international student insurance is required

title: Female Early Childhood Volunteer Athens, Greece
body:
Glocal Roots is a grassroots organisation operating in Greece and Switzerland since 2019, our solution: breaking the dependency cycle by building resilience and autonomy

We build structures and networks that support displaced people to become resilient, autonomous and self-reliant again!

Since April 2022 we are running a Women’s and Kid’s space together in Athens. Our child-friendly area provides a safe and fun space for children. It’s equipped with arts and crafts materials, a toy cooking station, a reading corner, and many toys to play with. In our kids’ space, we provide supervised child care for mothers and fathers who take part in services provided by our partner organizations or us in the Victoria Community Center. Activities include Greek, English and art classes, psychological and legal support sessions, and cafe space for parents to relax.

**Key responsibilities of the job include:**

- Providing appropriate support and guidance to children in the Kid’s space
- Providing social support including maintaining an environment that builds the confidence, resilience and self-esteem of children
- Motivating and encouraging children
- Prepare creative and simple activities for children to run in the space
- Attend weekly team meetings (depending on the number of shifts)
- Reporting any child or adult protection concerns to the Protection focal points
- Remaining flexible based on the project needs
- Cleaning of the spaces after your shift along with the rest of the volunteer team

**Your desired set of skills:**

- Experience in teaching, preferably in early childhood education
- An awareness and interest in migration issues and sensitivity to working with vulnerable communities
- Motivation and passion for working alongside a dynamic and hard-working team

Volunteers are responsible for covering transport costs to and from Athens. Shared accommodation with single rooms is provided in our volunteer flat for €12 per night.

*To apply, send an email to athens@glocalroots.org*

*Minimum commitment: 8 weeks. Ideal Commitment: 2+ month → for fulltime volunteers*
